info.title: Acuris Geo API
info.description:
REST API for **address validation**, **geocoding**, and **address suggestions**
across supported countries (see **Country codes** below).

**AI agents / MCP:** the same capabilities are exposed as self-describing MCP
tools at `https://api.acuris-geo.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP; authenticate with
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`). See [/docs/mcp](https://api.acuris-geo.com/docs/mcp).

### Authentication
Present your API key using any of the following (listed in priority order):
- **`X-Acuris-Key: <key>`** header — preferred for keys issued via Stripe Checkout.
- **`Authorization: Bearer <key>`** header — standard OAuth-style bearer; works for any key.
- **`X-API-Key: <key>`** header.
- **`?key=<key>`** query parameter (legacy).
- **`{"key": "..."}`** JSON body field on `POST /validate` (legacy).

Header auth is preferred: query-param secrets can leak into access logs, Referer
headers, and browser history. A `password` parameter is **not** an API-key
channel anywhere (query or body) — it is reserved for account login.

Without a key, **anonymous free tier** access is rate-limited per IP, and per-product
daily free limits apply. Check remaining free calls via `/validate-credits` and
`/geocode-credits`; see the pricing page at https://www.acuris-geo.com/acuris-pricing/ for details.
**This anonymous path is being retired for validate/geocode/reverse/postcode-lookup in favor of
requiring a free account** — see **Free tier (verified account)** below for the allowance you get
once you sign up, and the forthcoming anonymous-access change.

### Versioned namespace (`/v1/*`)
A stable, versioned `/v1/*` namespace mirrors the core endpoints (e.g. `/v1/validate`,
`/v1/validate/batch`, `/v1/geocode`, `/v1/reverse`). Behavior is identical to the unversioned
routes; prefer `/v1/*` for long-lived integrations. Details are documented on the individual
path items.

#### RapidAPI
When consumed via the RapidAPI marketplace, the RapidAPI gateway is the identity
provider: it injects `X-RapidAPI-Proxy-Secret` (a shared secret verified server-side),
`X-RapidAPI-Key`, `X-RapidAPI-User`, and `X-RapidAPI-Subscription` on every request.
Plan quotas are enforced upstream by RapidAPI; no Acuris account or transaction balance is required
for traffic routed through RapidAPI. Direct (non-RapidAPI) calls continue to use the
authentication methods above.

### Country codes (validation & geocode `country`)
We hold reference databases for **~250 countries**, roughly **130** of them
with house-number-level data, and a street-segment interpolation cascade
live in **~95 countries**. Full multi-tier precision (an address-level
reference DB plus the street-segment cascade) covers a flagship set
including `usa`, `can`, `gbr`, `deu`, `aut`, `che`, `fra`, `esp`, `bel`,
`nld`, `dnk`, `fin`, `swe`, `nor`, `ita`, `jpn`, `sgp`, among others.
The United Kingdom is served at full Royal Mail PAF precision (UPRN / UDPRN)
on its dedicated host — see **United Kingdom host** below. Belgium is fully
trilingual (NL / FR / DE).
The **acceptance set is far larger than the full-precision tier**: any country in the
`COUNTRY_GEOCODE` table validates (~223 live today, and growing), returning the
best tier its reference data supports — from a point coordinate down to an
admin-area centroid.
Inspect `accuracy_type` in each response to see which tier was returned for a
given lookup. Additional countries are being onboarded — see the roadmap on
[acuris-geo.com](https://www.acuris-geo.com/).

### United Kingdom host
All `country=gbr` traffic — `/validate`, `/suggest`, `/reverse`, and the
UK-only endpoints `/postcode-lookup` and `/geocode-uk` — is served from
**https://paf.acuris-geo.com** (see Servers). A `gbr` request sent to the
main host is refused rather than silently degraded: it returns **400**
`{"error": "country_not_served_by_this_endpoint", "use_instead": "https://paf.acuris-geo.com"}`.

### Free enrichment
Validated addresses in **eighteen countries** — USA, Canada, Germany,
Austria, Switzerland, France, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Spain, Portugal,
Ireland, the Netherlands, Finland, Sweden, Luxembourg, Japan, Singapore and
Hong Kong — automatically carry a free `enrichment` block of official
statistical geography (no extra charge, no request parameter); see the
`enrichment` property on `ValidateResponse` for the fields and the
precision gates.

### Free tier (verified account)
A verified account — any key with `key_class: free_av_geo`, which is what `POST /register` +
email verification grants by default — gets a **recurring, non-expiring daily allowance** for
address validation, geocoding, and reverse geocoding. This is **not** a depleting trial pool:
it never runs out and the account never expires (`trial_expires_at` is `null` for these keys).

- **1,000 requests per UTC day, one shared allowance** — `/validate`, `/geocode` (and its
  `/geocode-usa` alias), and `/reverse` all draw from the same single 1,000/day bucket (not one
  bucket per product), which resets at UTC midnight, for as long as the account exists.
- **The UK is excluded from the 1,000/day allowance and is metered separately, because Royal
  Mail PAF data is licensed per lookup and cannot ride the general allowance.** Any
  `country=gbr` request — on `/validate`, `/reverse`, or the UK-only `/postcode-lookup` and
  `/geocode-uk` endpoints, all served from `https://paf.acuris-geo.com` (see **United Kingdom
  host** above) — is capped at **5 per UTC day** for a registered key (anonymous UK callers:
  **3 per UTC day** per IP) instead, and never draws from or combines
  with the 1,000/day figure. See `uk_trial` (`cap` / `used` / `remaining`) on `GET /check-key`.
- **`/postcode-lookup` only ever serves `country=gbr`** — any other country is rejected before
  any transaction check runs — so it is always billed under the UK daily cap, **never** the
  1,000/day allowance, regardless of key class.
- **`/suggest` (autocomplete) has its own metering rules, never the UK daily
  cap described above — and its numbers depend on the same launch flag as the anonymous
  403 described below (`AV_GEO_REQUIRE_SIGNUP`, or the dedicated `AV_GEO_SUGGEST_METER` if
  set):**
    - **As of this writing, that flag is off in production**, so `/suggest` behaves as it has
      historically: a genuinely valid API key is completely exempt from metering here, and
      anonymous widget-token callers are bounded only by a per-IP flask-limiter soft cap of
      **5/second, 60/minute, 500/day** (per gunicorn worker — a first-line burst backstop,
      not an authoritative cross-fleet limit; the handler does not authenticate against a
      quota pool or decrement one in this state).
    - **Once the flag is switched on**, any genuinely valid key — other than the
      policy-exempt `stripe` / `integration` / `partner` classes, which stay unmetered — draws
      from the same shared recurring **1,000 requests per UTC day** allowance that
      `/validate`/`/geocode`/`/reverse` draw from (same bucket, same `free_remaining` field on
      a `200`), refused with `free_limit_reached` (`403`) once
      exhausted. Anonymous callers are capped at **40 per UTC day per IP** instead (refused
      with `rate_limit_exceeded`, `429`), and the flask-limiter decorator's daily figure drops
      from 500 to 40 at the same moment as a redundant first-line backstop. `country: "gbr"`
      requests draw from this SAME bucket, never the UK daily cap — see the `/suggest`
      operation below for why.
  `country: "gbr"` suggest requests carry one further, independent layer regardless of flag
  state — a per-IP anti-scrape velocity cap (`PAF_SUGGEST_IP_RPM`, **600/minute** by default,
  10x that for a genuinely valid non-test API key, allowlisted keys exempt) that degrades to
  an empty `{"suggestions": [], "limit": "reached"}` result rather than an error when tripped.
  See the `/suggest` operation below for the full contract.
- `GET /check-key` reports `key_class`, and for `free_av_geo` keys also `free_remaining`
  (a single integer: today's remaining count in the shared daily allowance) and
  `free_daily_limit` (`1000`). The legacy `validation_credits` / `geocode_credits` fields on these keys are a
  frozen signup-time snapshot, not a live balance — use `free_remaining` instead.
- **Commercial use of the free tier requires a permanent, visible attribution link back to
  acuris-geo.com** on any page or product that displays results derived from it — see the
  Terms of Service for the exact wording required.
- **Anonymous (no-key) access to these endpoints is being retired — not yet live in production.**
  Once the `AV_GEO_REQUIRE_SIGNUP` flag is enabled, a request to `/validate`, `/geocode`,
  `/reverse`, or `/postcode-lookup` with no API key at all will return **403**
  `{"error": "signup_required", "message": "Create a free account to use this endpoint — ..."}`
  instead of being served under the anonymous per-IP daily limits described under
  **Authentication** above, directing the caller to register for the allowance described here.
  As of this writing that flag is **off** in production: anonymous per-IP limits still apply
  exactly as documented above until it is switched on.

### Match quality contract (validate and geocode)
Every successful or not-found response carries a machine-readable precision tier:
- **`accuracy_type`** — what the returned coordinate represents. **This is an
  OPEN set**: new tiers are added as reference data improves, so pass
  unrecognized values through rather than treating them as a failure.
  *Point coordinates* (a coordinate for one address): `rooftop` (a point on
  the building) and `arrival_point` (its entrance / gate / curb-side access
  point). *Derived tiers* (a segment or an area, not an address):
  `street_interpolated` (HNO estimated along a street-segment polyline),
  `street_segment_centroid` (street confirmed, exact HNO not in DB; the pin is
  the centre of the known house numbers nearest the one typed),
  `street_centroid` (street confirmed, exact HNO not in DB; the pin is the
  middle of the street),
  `postcode_centroid`, `locality_centroid`, `admin_centroid`. `null` on
  `no_match`.
- **`point_coordinate`** — boolean; `true` for `rooftop` and `arrival_point`,
  `false` for every derived tier. **Branch on this rather than on
  `accuracy_type` string literals** — a literal comparison silently
  reclassifies each newly-added tier as imprecise. Not yet emitted by
  `/reverse` — derive it from `accuracy_type` there.
- `match_type` — internal/legacy tier with a numeric score table:
  `rooftop` (1.0), `parcel_centroid` (0.9), `interpolated` (0.8),
  `street_level` (0.6), `zip_centroid` (0.4), `city_centroid` (0.2), `no_match` (0.0).
  Retained for backward compat; `accuracy_type` is the recommended field.
- `match_score` — float `0.0`–`1.0` mirroring `match_type`.
- `match_components` — object indicating which input fields were confirmed by the match.
- `input_corrected` — `true` when any input field was normalized or corrected.

**Cascade behavior on geocode:** when the addresses DB has no rooftop record for the
submitted address, the engine falls back to a street-segment DB (SEG) and emits the
highest-precision tier available (interpolated → street centroid → postcode centroid →
locality centroid). `/validate` follows the same cascade for the returned `lat`/`lng`,
but `confidence_level` (high/medium/low/none) reflects whether the address was *confirmed*,
not where the coordinate came from — SEG-derived results stay at low/none since SEG can attest
to plausibility but not existence.

Validation also exposes:
- `suggestions` — ranked near-misses when exact match fails, or alternates when a fuzzy match succeeds.
- `alternative_matches` — same street + house number found in a different state (USA / CAN only).
- `reasons` — failure classifications (`street_not_found`, `city_not_matching`, `locality_unknown`).
  For Portugal, `street_not_found` can also appear on a 200 `approximate` town-level answer.
  On centroid-fallback responses, `reasons` also includes a `validation_failed:*` marker explaining
  which validator/matcher error triggered the fallback.
- `partial_match` — `true` when the address itself could not be validated against the DB but the
  cascade still inferred a centroid coordinate (postcode / locality / admin). Always inspect this
  before claiming an address is "valid and deliverable": `partial_match: true` means only the
  coordinate is trustworthy, the address fields were not confirmed.
- `match_type_legacy` / `match_score_legacy` — retained for backward compatibility with pre-2026 clients
  (old values: `exact` / `fuzzy`, and the string label `"Perfect match"`, etc.).

### Centroid-fallback on `/validate`
When the v1/v2 lookup cannot match the input against the addresses DB (`street_not_found`,
or required fields like `street` are missing but a postcode/locality is present),
`/validate` falls through to the SEG cascade and — if a `postcode_centroid` / `locality_centroid` / `admin_centroid`
can be inferred — returns **200** with `lat`/`lng` set, `accuracy_type` populated, and `partial_match: true`.
If SEG also has nothing usable, the original **404** (or **400** for missing-required-field) is returned unchanged.
This means a 200 response no longer *necessarily* means the address itself validated — always check `partial_match`.

### HTTP status codes
- **200** match found, **or** centroid-fallback returned (`partial_match: true`, see below).
- **400** missing required field (e.g. `country`). On `/validate` a missing `street`/`city` only returns 400 when SEG also has nothing — otherwise a 200 centroid-fallback is returned. Also returned for `country=gbr` requests sent to the main host instead of the PAF host (`country_not_served_by_this_endpoint`, with `use_instead`).
- **401** invalid or inactive API key.
- **402** payment required — subscription canceled or a prepaid transaction pack expired (paid data endpoints).
- **403** insufficient transaction balance, trial expired, or anonymous limit reached.
  When a free **daily** allowance is used up — `free_limit_reached` (the shared 1,000/day
  allowance) or `uk_trial_cap_reached` (the UK Royal Mail PAF daily cap) — the body also
  carries `resets_at` (ISO 8601 UTC, the next UTC midnight, e.g. `2026-10-09T00:00:00Z`) and
  `retry_after_seconds` (integer, at least 1), the response has a standard `Retry-After`
  header with the same number of seconds, and `message` states the reset time in UTC plus UK
  (and, for `free_limit_reached`, Germany) local time. Error codes, status and the existing
  fields (`free_remaining`, `uk_trial_cap` / `uk_trial_used` / `uk_trial_remaining`,
  `key_accepted`) are unchanged.
- **404** address not found **and** the SEG cascade had no centroid to offer. Body still includes `match_type: "no_match"`, plus `suggestions` and `reasons` when available.
- **422** input could not be parsed (e.g. `input` was neither a string nor an object on `/validate`).
- **429** rate limit exceeded (`rate_limit_exceeded`).
- **501** reverse geocoding not yet enabled for this country (spatial index missing).
- **503** reference database not available on this deployment.
- **504** validation timed out.

Human-friendly **register / login** flows: HTML pages at `/register` and `/login` (browser). Obtain an API key from the customer dashboard after signup at [acuris-geo.com/dashboard](https://www.acuris-geo.com/dashboard).

servers.description: United Kingdom (PAF) — all country=gbr requests are served here

post.description:
Accepts a single-line address string **or** structured fields in `input`,
plus required `country` (ISO-style code).

**Body formats:** JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) is the documented
format. A form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) or `multipart/form-data`
body with the same flat field names (`country`, `street`, `city`, ...) is also
accepted, and `country_code` / `countryCode` are accepted as aliases of `country`.
Address fields are never read from the query string.

**Street-level answers (Netherlands):** a street sent without a house number (or
with one that is not on file) is answered at street level (`street_centroid`,
`street_segment_centroid`, `street_interpolated`). Such an answer lists the
postcodes the street covers in `street_postcodes`; when there is more than one,
`postcode_range` and `standardized.postcode` state the range as `from 9573 PA to
9573 PH`, and `standardized.formatted_address` prints it with two spaces before the
town (PostNL convention). A street sent with no city that exists in several places
is refused with the count and a request to add a city or postcode (see
`ValidateErrorBody.locality_count`); when a postcode was sent but is not on
file, the message asks for a city only.

**Postcode + house number (Netherlands):** `postcode` (PC6, e.g. `3999 NN`,
`3999NN` or `3999 nn`) and `house_number` alone, with no street and no city, is
a complete Dutch address and is accepted (single line too: `3999 NN 27`). When
exactly one street holds that number at that postcode, the answer is that
address (`rooftop`, status `verified`, `corrections: []`) and the derived parts
are disclosed with `street_backfilled_from_postcode: true` and
`city_backfilled_from_postcode: true` (they are not corrections: nothing you sent
was wrong). A letter (huisletter, `17a`) selects that letter's own address. When
several streets hold the number at that postcode the request is a 404 with
`reasons: ["street_missing", "postcode_house_number_ambiguous"]` and
`did_you_mean` entries (`street`, `city`, `postcode`, `house_number`; at most 6).
When the number exists only with letters (`3A`, `3B`, ...) and none was sent, the
answer adds reason `house_number_extension_missing` and lists the letters in
`did_you_mean`. A number not on file at that postcode is answered at the
postcode (`postcode_centroid`, `partial_match: true`, reason
`house_number_not_in_reference`, empty `standardized.street`), never with a
400. A street or city you send is used as sent (this lookup does not run).

**Credits:** A validation costs **1 Stripe-plan transaction** (`validate=1`). The trial
pool decrements **1** regardless of endpoint weight. Anonymous callers consume one
free slot per IP (per-product daily free limits apply — check remaining via
`/validate-credits`; anonymous access is rate-limited per IP).

**Response add-ons (opt-in):**
- **ISO 20022 / CBPR+** — pass `"iso20022": true` in the body (or `?iso20022=1`)
  to add an `iso20022` block mapping the result onto Swift CBPR+ postal-address
  shapes (`structured` / `hybrid`) plus explicit truth `assertions`, hard-negative
  `refutation`s, and `unresolved` coverage gaps. Opt-in/**beta**; the default
  response shape is unchanged when the flag is absent. See `Iso20022Block`.
  The flag also switches PO-box handling: without it, non-deliverable input is
  rejected with 400; with `iso20022: true` it is accepted and labelled via
  `non_deliverable_type` (ISO 20022 postal addresses may be PO boxes).
- **`mode=interactive` (AD-parity resolver)** — pass `"mode": "interactive"` with a
  **fielded** `input` object to get a ranked pick-list / valid house-number-range
  envelope (`process_status`, `results[]`) instead of the single batch verdict.
  Opt-in/**beta**; billed identically to a batch validation (1 transaction). The default
  `mode: batch` contract is untouched. See `InteractiveEnvelope`.

200.description:
Validation succeeded **or** partial fallback returned. Inspect `partial_match`
to distinguish: when `true`, the address was not fully confirmed — either the
street resolved but not the house number (`street_interpolated` /
`street_centroid`), or the SEG cascade inferred a `postcode_centroid` /
`locality_centroid` / `admin_centroid` for `lat`/`lng`. `reasons` states what
could not be pinned down.

400.description:
Missing country, unsupported country, or bad payload. A missing `street`/`city`
only surfaces as 400 when the SEG cascade also has no centroid to offer — when SEG
can supply one, a 200 with `partial_match: true` is returned instead. Netherlands:
`postcode` + `house_number` with no street and no city is never a 400 (see the
Netherlands postcode + house number note in the `/validate` description). Portugal: a
street without a city is a 404 (see below), not a 400; a city-only request
returns a labelled approximate 200 (`approximate: true`) when the place is
found. Also returned
for `country: gbr` requests sent to this host — the UK is served from
`https://paf.acuris-geo.com` (body: `country_not_served_by_this_endpoint`
with `use_instead`).

Also returned for **non-deliverable input** (PO Box, Postfach, Rural Route, …):
the body then carries the full match-quality contract with
`match_type: "non_deliverable"`, `non_deliverable_type` (e.g. `po_box`) and
`reasons: ["non_deliverable_address"]` — see `MatchType`. With `iso20022: true`
the same input is instead accepted as a labelled 200 (`non_deliverable_type` on
the success body), since ISO 20022 postal addresses may legitimately be PO boxes.

Payment required (Stripe-plan keys): `subscription_canceled`,
`pack_expired` (body includes `expired_at`), or `credits_wrong_region`
(body includes `country`, `have_regions`, `needed` — the key's credit
packs do not cover the requested country's region).

403.description:
Insufficient transaction balance. Body shapes: `{"error": "quota_exceeded", "pool", "limit",
"used", "message"}` for exhausted plan quota; trial keys return
`{"error": "insufficient_credits" | "trial_expired", "key_accepted": true,
"credits_remaining", "validation_credits_remaining", "geocode_credits_remaining"}`.
Key-level 403s: `{"error": "key_blocked", "message"}` when the
API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

404.description:
Address not found **and** SEG cascade had no centroid to offer. Body includes
`match_type: no_match`, `suggestions` (if any near-misses scored ≥ 0.5), and `reasons`.
When SEG _does_ have a centroid, the response is 200 with `partial_match: true`
instead of 404.

Portugal (`country: prt`): `reasons` names the cause (e.g. `city_not_found`,
`street_not_found`, `street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing`,
`locality_ambiguous` + `street_missing`), and `did_you_mean` lists what the input
most likely meant (never applied automatically) — alongside the unchanged
`suggestions`. A street sent without a city returns this 404 (with the candidate
towns in `did_you_mean`) rather than a 400, unless exactly one town holds the
street, in which case that town is used and disclosed as a `City` correction.

422.description: Input could not be parsed (e.g. `input` was neither a string nor an object).

Returns how many **free** validations remain for this IP today (UTC-based server tracking).
Per-product daily free limits apply; anonymous access is rate-limited per IP. Use this
(and `/geocode-credits`) to read the remaining free allowance before it is exhausted.

get.description:
Provide `country` and either a single-line `q` or fielded address
components. Resolution runs the same parse → infer → lookup chain
`/validate` uses — if `/validate` can place an input, `/geocode`
places it, by construction. **No component is required at the
gate**: `street`, `city`/`town` and `state` are all optional,
including for USA and Canada. Omitting `street` degrades the match
to a locality/postcode tier rather than failing.

**Portugal (`country=prt`):** a city-only or neighbourhood-only
request (no street) returns a **labelled approximate point**: a 200
with `approximate: true`, `resolved_level`, `resolved_name`, reason
`street_missing`, `accuracy_type` `locality_centroid` or
`admin_centroid`. A place name that is a
locality in several municipalities is never guessed: 404 with
`reasons: ["locality_ambiguous", "street_missing"]` and the
candidates in `did_you_mean`. A place name not found at all returns
400 `Missing required field: street`. A street sent without a city
is placed when exactly one town holds it (the town is filled in);
otherwise the 404 lists the candidate towns in `did_you_mean`. When
the street cannot be placed in the town sent, the town centre may be
served with `approximate: true` and reason `fell_back_to_locality`.
This includes an estate, urbanisation or neighbourhood name sent with
a town we can place (for example "Cerrado do Poço" in Porto Salvo),
or with the town as the last words of the text and no city field
(for example "Tapada Vale dos Lobos Belas"):
the 200 is a labelled town-level point, and its `reasons` then carry
`street_not_found` next to `fell_back_to_locality`. A street-type name
(Rua, Avenida, ...) that is not found, or a name sent with an
ambiguous or unknown town, stays a 404.
When the house number is not in the reference data, the 200 carries
`nearby_house_numbers` (see `ForwardGeocodeResponse`).

A single-line free-text address may be passed as `q` instead of the
fielded parameters; it is parsed with the same parser the `/validate`
path uses. This works for every supported country, including the
eight (aus, bra, can, jpn, mex, mys, tur, usa) that used to require
fielded `street`/`city`/`state` and 400 on single-line input.
Explicit fielded parameters, when present, take precedence over the
parsed single line.

**Response vocabulary:** the response is a whitelist of
geocoding-only fields — `lat`, `lng`, `accuracy_type`,
`point_coordinate`, `standardized`, `formatted_address`, and,
conditionally, `arrival_point`, `input_modified`, `attribution`,
`uprn` and `digipin`. See `ForwardGeocodeResponse` below. It never carries the
`/validate` verdict vocabulary (`status`, `match_type`,
`match_score`, `confidence`, `corrections`, and similar fields) — a
miss is a plain `{"error": "no_match", "message": "..."}` body, not
a verdict with everything zeroed out.

**Credits:** A geocode costs **1 Stripe-plan transaction** (`geocode=1`). Combined AV+GEO pool since 2026-07-23: an address validation costs one transaction and includes coordinates at no extra cost; a standalone geocode also costs one transaction, from the same plan allowance. The trial
pool decrements **1** regardless of endpoint weight. Anonymous callers consume one
free slot per IP (per-product daily free limits apply — check remaining via
`/geocode-credits`).

get.description:
Finds the nearest known address to a given `lat`/`lng` within `radius_m` metres
from the reference database. Results are sorted by distance ascending and include
a `distance_m` field.

**Credits:** Stripe-plan keys are charged a flat **1 transaction per request**
(`reverse=1`), regardless of `limit`. Trial/dev keys are charged **1 transaction per
returned address**, pre-capped to the remaining balance so the call never
overdraws. `units_charged` in the response echoes the number of addresses
returned (which equals the trial-key debit; the Stripe debit is always 1).

**RapidAPI note:** For traffic routed through the RapidAPI gateway, `limit`
is forced server-side to **1** so that one HTTP request maps to exactly one
`Geocoding Lookups` meter decrement. The `limit` query parameter is silently
ignored for RapidAPI clients.

**Availability:** Available for ~160 countries. Availability is detected per
country from the reference DB — any DB carrying an `(RT_LAT, RT_LNG)`-leading
rooftop-coordinate index serves reverse, and the set expands automatically when
an index lands. Countries without it return **501** `reverse_not_available` —
currently including `che`, `jpn`, `tur`, `kor`, `isr`, `arg`, `chl`, `vnm`,
`pak`, `phl`, `hkg`; `gbr` reverse is served via the PAF host.

parameters.description:
Max results to return. Capped at `10`.
**Ignored for RapidAPI traffic** — forced to `1` to align with the
per-request `Geocoding Lookups` meter.

Match found. When `limit=1` (default) the body is a single result;

"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

get.description:
Autocomplete/typeahead. Returns ranked standardized addresses (with
`formatted_address`, and `lat`/`lng` whenever the reference row carries
a coordinate — never invented) for the partial input `q` (or `prefix`)
and `country`.

**Authentication is required — there is no anonymous access.** A caller
must present *either*:
  - a paid API key (Stripe `X-Acuris-Key` / `Authorization: Bearer`,
    `X-API-Key`, or RapidAPI gateway) — full access, billed against the
    key's own transaction pool; or
  - a short-lived **widget token** (`X-Acuris-Widget-Token` header, or
    `?t=`) minted by `/widget/token` — origin-locked to `acuris-geo.com`
    pages, so not usable by third-party integrations (partners use API
    keys). Widget callers are capped at 15 results and a per-token call
    quota.

Requests with neither are rejected: `403` (no widget origin / no token)
or `401` (token invalid, expired, or quota exhausted).

**Metering here depends on the `AV_GEO_REQUIRE_SIGNUP` launch flag** (see **Free tier
(verified account)** above for the full explanation — this endpoint never draws from the
UK daily cap described there, on either side of the flag, and draws from the 1,000/day
free-tier allowance only once the flag is on):
  - **As of this writing, flag off in production:** a genuinely valid API key is
    completely exempt from metering. Anonymous widget-token callers are bounded only by a
    per-IP flask-limiter soft cap of **5/second, 60/minute, 500/day** (per gunicorn
    worker — a first-line burst backstop, not an authoritative cross-fleet limit); the
    handler does not authenticate against a quota pool or decrement one in this state.
  - **Once the flag is on:** a registered key (any class except the policy-exempt
    `stripe`/`integration`/`partner`) draws from the same shared recurring
    **1,000/day** allowance as `/validate`/`/geocode`/`/reverse` (`free_limit_reached`, `403`, once exhausted); anonymous callers are capped at
    **40/day per IP** instead (`rate_limit_exceeded`, `429`, once exhausted), and the
    flask-limiter decorator's daily figure drops from 500 to 40 at the same moment as a
    redundant first-line backstop.
`country: "gbr"` requests carry one further, independent per-IP velocity cap
(`PAF_SUGGEST_IP_RPM`, **600/minute** by default — 10x that for a genuinely valid, non-test
API key; allowlisted keys exempt), which degrades to an empty result set
(`{"suggestions": [], "limit": "reached"}`) rather than an error, on either side of the flag.

**UK note:** `country: "gbr"` is served exclusively from
`https://paf.acuris-geo.com` (identical path, parameters, and auth).
Requests for `gbr` sent to `api.acuris-geo.com` return **400**
`{"error": "country_not_served_by_this_endpoint", "country": "gbr",
"use_instead": "https://paf.acuris-geo.com"}`.

**Postcode-first input:** the query may lead with (or be) a postal
code. GBR: a full or partial postcode returns every delivery point at
that postcode, each labelled with `building_name` /
`organisation_name` / `department`; a premise name may precede the
postcode (`Gate House DL12 0NQ`). DEU / FIN / SWE / NLD / CAN: a
leading postcode scopes the street search (`67549 Eckenbert`,
`M5V 3L9`). JPN: a postcode returns chōme suggestions; then pass
`zip`, `oaza`, `chome` with the house-number keystrokes to get
banchi-gō lot suggestions.

Suggestions do not carry `udprn` / `uprn` / `county`. To obtain the
Royal Mail / OS identifiers for a chosen suggestion, submit it to
`/validate` (returns `uprn`, `udprn`) or use `/postcode-lookup`.

Suggestion `lat`/`lng` are the reference row's own point, unrefined.
`/validate` may refine that point for the same address (France: a
point lying just outside its building is moved onto the building
footprint, by at most 8 m, and the response carries
`coord_snapped: true`). List rows never carry that refinement; for
the refined point, submit the chosen suggestion to `/validate`.

Typeahead is tuned and verified for **19 countries** today — GBR, USA,
CAN, DEU, AUT, CHE, FRA, BEL, NLD, LUX, DNK, SWE, FIN, IRL, PRT, ESP,
SGP, JPN, HKG. Any `/geocode` country code is accepted; countries
outside this set may return empty results.

Returns every delivery point at a given UK postcode, backed by the official
Royal Mail Postcode Address File (PAF). **UK-only** (`country: "gbr"`). Each
address carries the Royal Mail `udprn`, the Ordnance Survey `uprn` (with its
`uprn_match_m` match distance), the full printable PAF element set
(`post_town`, dependent localities, `address_lines`, `administrative_county`),
and rooftop coordinates when available.

**UK host:** call this endpoint on `https://paf.acuris-geo.com`. Requests
sent to `api.acuris-geo.com` return **400**
`{"error": "country_not_served_by_this_endpoint", "use_instead": "https://paf.acuris-geo.com"}`.

are returned. Anonymous callers use the free tier (per-IP daily cap). The
number of addresses returned is capped (default 100); when the cap is hit
the response sets `truncated: true`. A per-IP velocity cap also applies to
protect the licensed dataset.

API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

Versioned alias of `POST /validate` — same handler, same request/response
shapes, same billing. Accepts a single-line address string **or** structured
fields in `input`, plus required `country`. The API key may be supplied in the

decrements **1** regardless. Anonymous callers consume one free slot per IP
(per-product daily free limits apply — check remaining via `/validate-credits`;

to distinguish: when `true`, the address was not fully confirmed — either the
street resolved but not the house number (`street_interpolated` /
`street_centroid`), or the SEG cascade inferred a `postcode_centroid` /
`locality_centroid` / `admin_centroid` for `lat`/`lng`. `reasons` states what
could not be pinned down.

400.description:
Missing country, unsupported country, or bad payload. A missing `street`/`city`
only surfaces as 400 when the SEG cascade also has no centroid to offer — when SEG
can supply one, a 200 with `partial_match: true` is returned instead. Netherlands:
`postcode` + `house_number` with no street and no city is never a 400 (see the
Netherlands postcode + house number note in the `/validate` description). Portugal: a
street without a city is a 404 (see below), not a 400; a city-only request
returns a labelled approximate 200 (`approximate: true`) when the place is
found. Also returned
for `country: gbr` requests sent to this host — the UK is served from
`https://paf.acuris-geo.com` (body: `country_not_served_by_this_endpoint`
with `use_instead`).

Also returned for **non-deliverable input** (PO Box, Postfach, Rural Route, …):
the body then carries the full match-quality contract with
`match_type: "non_deliverable"`, `non_deliverable_type` (e.g. `po_box`) and
`reasons: ["non_deliverable_address"]` — see `MatchType`. With `iso20022: true`
the same input is instead accepted as a labelled 200 (`non_deliverable_type` on
the success body).

402.description:
Payment required (Stripe-plan keys): `subscription_canceled`,
`pack_expired` (body includes `expired_at`), or `credits_wrong_region`
(body includes `country`, `have_regions`, `needed`).

403.description:
Insufficient transaction balance. Body shapes: `{"error": "quota_exceeded", "pool", "limit",
"used", "message"}` for exhausted plan quota; trial keys return
`{"error": "insufficient_credits" | "trial_expired", "key_accepted": true,
"credits_remaining", "validation_credits_remaining", "geocode_credits_remaining"}`.
Key-level 403s: `{"error": "key_blocked", "message"}` when the
API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

404.description:
Address not found **and** SEG cascade had no centroid to offer. Body includes
`match_type: no_match`, `suggestions` (if any near-misses scored ≥ 0.5), and `reasons`.
When SEG _does_ have a centroid, the response is 200 with `partial_match: true`
instead of 404.

Portugal (`country: prt`): `reasons` names the cause (e.g. `city_not_found`,
`street_not_found`, `street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing`,
`locality_ambiguous` + `street_missing`), and `did_you_mean` lists what the input
most likely meant (never applied automatically) — alongside the unchanged
`suggestions`. A street sent without a city returns this 404 (with the candidate
towns in `did_you_mean`) rather than a 400, unless exactly one town holds the
street, in which case that town is used and disclosed as a `City` correction.

422.description: Input could not be parsed (e.g. `input` was neither a string nor an object).

post.summary: Validate up to 200 addresses in one request (versioned alias)
post.description:
Synchronous bulk validation. Each row is billed and matched exactly as a
standalone `POST /validate` call would be (`validate=1` transaction each). An
**API key is required** — the free-tier per-IP allowance is for single
`POST /validate` only.

Every row shares the top-level `country` unless the row is an object of the
form `{"input": <input>, "country": "usa"}`, which overrides the country for
that row (letting you mix countries in one batch). For volumes above 200,
submit an async job via `POST /validate/jobs` (up to 50,000 addresses).

200.description:
Per-row results, in request order. Each element is the same body a
standalone `POST /validate` would return (including per-row `error`
objects for rows that failed).

400.description: `addresses` is not an array, is empty, or exceeds 200 entries (`batch_too_large`).

401.description: API key required (`api_key_required`) — batch has no anonymous free tier.

post.summary: Geocode an address (versioned alias, JSON body)
post.description:
Versioned alias of `GET /geocode` — same handler, same response shape, same
billing. Accepts the geocode parameters as a JSON body instead of a query
string (scalar body fields are folded onto the query params; query-string
values win on collision). In addition to the fielded parameters, this alias
accepts a single-line free-text address as `q`, which is parsed into
components with the same parser the `/validate` path uses (explicit fielded
params take precedence over the parsed line). `q` also works on
`GET /geocode`; and `GET /v1/geocode` with the same query parameters as the
unversioned route is accepted too.

**Credits:** `geocode=1` Stripe-plan transaction per call. Combined AV+GEO pool since 2026-07-23: an address validation costs one transaction and includes coordinates at no extra cost; a standalone geocode also costs one transaction, from the same plan allowance. The trial pool
decrements **1** regardless. Anonymous callers consume one free slot per IP
(per-product daily free limits apply — check remaining via `/geocode-credits`;
anonymous access is rate-limited per IP).

q.description: Single-line free-text address, parsed into components.

postalcode.description: Postcode. The aliases `postcode`, `zip`, `zipcode`, `zip_code` and `postal_code` are also accepted; `postalcode` wins when several are sent.

key.description: API key in the body (legacy; folded onto `?key=`). Header auth is preferred.

db_version.description: Ignored. Reference DBs are configured at server startup via ref_dbs.json.

200.description: Geocode result — a whitelist of geocoding-only fields. See `GET /geocode` for worked examples.

400.description: Missing/unsupported `country`, or neither `q` nor any fielded component supplied Portugal: also `Missing required field: street` for a city-only request whose place name is not found.

403.description:
Invalid key, no transaction balance, or anonymous geocode limit reached.
Key-level 403s: `{"error": "key_blocked", "message"}` when the
API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

404.description: No match. Body is `{"error": "no_match", "message": "..."}` — never the `/validate` match-quality contract (no `match_type`, `match_score`, `match_components`, `input_corrected`). Portugal: may also carry `reasons`, `did_you_mean` and `did_you_mean_truncated` (see `ForwardGeocodeErrorBody`).

422.description: Input could not be interpreted. Same `{"error": "no_match", "message": "..."}` shape as 404.

500.description: Internal error during geocoding. Body: `{"error": "Internal error"}`.

503.description: Reference database not available, or another engine-level failure.

post.description:
Versioned alias of `GET /reverse` — same handler, same response shape, same
billing. Accepts `lat`/`lng`/`radius_m`/`limit`/`country` as a JSON body
instead of a query string (scalar body fields are folded onto the query
params; query-string values win on collision). Results are sorted by distance
ascending and include a `distance_m` field.

**Credits:** Stripe-plan keys: flat `reverse=1` transaction per request, regardless
of `limit`. Trial/dev keys: 1 transaction per returned address, pre-capped to the
remaining balance. `units_charged` echoes the number of addresses returned
(equals the trial-key debit; the Stripe debit is always 1).

**Availability:** Available for ~160 countries. Detected per country from the
reference DB (rooftop-coordinate index) and expands automatically; countries
without it return **501** `reverse_not_available` — currently including
`che`, `jpn`, `tur`, `kor`, `isr`, `arg`, `chl`, `vnm`, `pak`, `phl`,
`hkg`; `gbr` reverse is served via the PAF host.

`GET /v1/reverse` with the same query parameters as the unversioned route
is also accepted.

radius_m.description: Search radius in metres. Capped at `50000`.

limit.description:
Max results to return. Capped at `10`.
**Ignored for RapidAPI traffic** — forced to `1`.

200.description:
Match found. When `limit=1` (default) the body is a single result;
when `limit>1` the body wraps `results: []` with `count`.

400.description: Missing/invalid country, lat, lng, radius_m, or limit

403.description:
Insufficient transaction balance, trial expired, or anonymous limit reached.
Key-level 403s: `{"error": "key_blocked", "message"}` when the
API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

404.description: No address within `radius_m`. Body includes `match_type: no_match` and `reasons: ["no_address_within_radius"]`.

501.description: Reverse geocoding not available for this country (`reverse_not_available`).

get.description:
Backward-compatible wrapper for `/geocode?country=gbr`. Provide `town`,
`street` and `hno`; matches against the Royal Mail PAF reference data and
returns rooftop coordinates plus the PAF `udprn` (Unique Delivery Point
Reference Number) and, when the address matches OS Open UPRN, the `uprn`
(Unique Property Reference Number). These are surfaced as extra fields on
the `GeocodeResponse` body.

**Credits:** This endpoint currently authenticates at the **default**
Stripe-plan transaction amount (`1`); the trial pool decrements **1** regardless
of endpoint weight. Billing parity with `/geocode-usa` (`geocode=1`) is
**pending** and will be aligned in a later release. Anonymous callers
consume one free slot per IP — per-product daily free limits apply
(check remaining via `/geocode-credits`); anonymous access is
rate-limited per IP.

**UK host:** call this endpoint on `https://paf.acuris-geo.com`. Requests
sent to `api.acuris-geo.com` return **400**
`{"error": "country_not_served_by_this_endpoint", "use_instead": "https://paf.acuris-geo.com"}`.

parameters.name: hno
parameters.description: House number

parameters.name: town
parameters.description: Post town

200.description: Geocode result with coordinates and `accuracy_type` precision tier. For UK matches the body also carries `udprn` and (when available) `uprn`.

400.description: Missing parameters (town, street and house number are required)

403.description:
Limit or transaction balance.
Key-level 403s: `{"error": "key_blocked", "message"}` when the
API key has been blocked (the `message` says why), and `{"error": "ip_not_allowed",
"message", "ip"}` when the key is restricted to approved source IP addresses and
this request came from another one (`ip` is the address we saw). Source-IP
restriction is optional and set up per key on request via support.

404.description: Address not found. Body carries `match_type: no_match`, zeroed `match_score`, and a full-false `match_components`.

503.description: Reference database not available on this deployment

post.summary: Validate up to 200 addresses in one request
post.description:
Synchronous bulk variant of `/validate`. Each address is fanned out
in-process to the real `POST /validate` route, so every result — and its
billing — is byte-identical to a standalone call. **Billing is per row:**
each address consumes one address-validation transaction (Stripe-plan transaction;
the trial pool decrements 1 regardless). There is **no submit-time `403`** —
if the key runs out of transactions, is over quota, or is invalid, that surfaces
inside the individual result entry rather than failing the whole batch.
**Requires an API key** (the anonymous free-tier IP path is for `POST /validate`
only). For larger volumes, submit an async job via `POST /validate/jobs`.

addresses.description:
Each entry is either an `input` (same single-line string or
fielded object as `POST /validate`), or an object
`{"input": <input>, "country": "usa"}` to override the batch
`country` per row. (`address` is accepted as an alias of `input`.)

country.description: Default ISO-style country code applied to rows without their own `country`.

200.description:
Per-address results. Individual entries may themselves carry an error
(e.g. `insufficient_validation_credits`) — inspect each result.

400.description: Missing/empty `addresses`, not an array, or more than 200 entries (use `POST /validate/jobs`).

401.description: API key required — batch validation is not available on the anonymous free tier.

post.summary: Submit an async address-validation job (up to 50,000)
post.description:
Queue a large address list for **asynchronous** validation — the path for
lists larger than the 200-address synchronous `/validate/batch` cap.
Returns a `job_id` immediately (HTTP 202); poll
`GET /validate/jobs/{job_id}` for status and results, or pass `webhook_url`
and the server POSTs `{job_id, status, addresses_count}` when processing
finishes. **Billing is per row inside the worker** — each address consumes
one address-validation transaction (Stripe-plan transaction; the trial pool
decrements 1 regardless), so there is **no submit-time `402`/`403`**. If the
account runs out of transactions partway through, the remaining results carry an
error entry rather than failing the whole job. **Requires an API key.** Runs
on the main box only (the UK PAF satellite returns `503` with a redirect hint).

addresses.description: Each entry is the same shape as `POST /validate`'s `input` (or `{"input": ..., "country": ...}` per-row override).

country.description: Default ISO-style country code for the job. Required.

webhook_url.description: Optional http(s) URL to receive a completion callback.

status_url.description: URL to poll for status / results.

400.description: Empty list, more than 50,000 addresses, missing `country`, or a non-http(s) `webhook_url`.

503.description: Submitted to the UK PAF satellite; resubmit to the main box (hint in body).

get.description:
Returns the job's status and, once `status` is `done`, the per-address
`results` (each byte-identical to a `POST /validate` response). The API key
must own the job.

200.description: Job status (with results when done).

404.description: Job not found, or the job belongs to a different key.

503.description: Queried on the UK PAF satellite; retry against the main box (hint in body).

get.description:
The true per-key quota endpoint for the logged-in console/dashboard.
Returns all four transaction pools with their denominators, the real trial
countdown, and Stripe subscription state — reflecting reality on load
and after each call (not the frozen login-fragment snapshot).

**Auth:** the account's own API key — send `X-Acuris-Key: <key>`
(primary). `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `X-API-Key`, or the legacy
`?key=` query param is also accepted.

**Transaction costs (Stripe-plan transactions, per call):** `validate` = 1,
`geocode` = 1, `reverse` = 1. During a trial the pool
decrements 1 regardless of endpoint weight.

Per-product daily free limits apply (check remaining via
`/validate-credits` and `/geocode-credits`); anonymous access is
rate-limited per IP.

200.description: Live balances, trial countdown, and subscription state for the caller's key.

401.description: API key required, or invalid/inactive key. Body includes `key_accepted: false`.

get.description:
Per-account usage for the console: the caller's most recent calls plus
7-day daily counts, for the caller's own API key. Summary fields only
(never the request payload). A fresh account returns empty arrays.

**Auth:** the account's own API key — send `X-Acuris-Key: <key>`
(primary). `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `X-API-Key`, or the legacy
`?key=` query param is also accepted.

200.description: Recent calls and 7-day daily usage counts for the caller's key.

401.description: API key required, or invalid/inactive key.

post.description:
**Recommended way to start.** Mints a low-cap, short-lived evaluation
key in one step — no password, no email round-trip, no free-domain
block. The key is returned directly in the response body.

The key seeds ~100 transactions in **each** pool (validation, geocode —
separate pools) and expires after **7 days**. These
are trial-pool credits: the pool decrements **1 per call** regardless of
endpoint. (Under a paid Stripe plan the same endpoints instead cost
weighted transactions — e.g. validate=1, geocode=1, reverse=1.)

Rate-limited to 1 issuance per email and 1 per IP in any 24-hour window
(and 60 requests/hour per IP overall). For more headroom, use the full
`/register` flow (28-day trial). Per-product daily free limits apply to
anonymous use — check remaining via `/validate-credits` and
`/geocode-credits`; anonymous access is also rate-limited per IP.

email.description: A valid email address to associate with the key. Free providers (Gmail etc.) are accepted.

country.description:
Optional ISO country hint (e.g. `gbr`). Drives the returned
`info_url` and, for `gbr`, adds a `paf_note` about UK
(Royal Mail PAF) evaluation limits.

200.description: Evaluation key issued. Send it as `X-Acuris-Key: <key>` (or `Authorization: Bearer`, `X-API-Key`, or `?key=`) on subsequent calls.

429.description:
Rate limited — a dev key was already issued to this email
(`error: rate_limited_email`) or from this IP
(`error: rate_limited_ip`) in the last 24 hours, or the hourly
request limit was exceeded.

500.description: Could not issue dev key (`error: internal`).

bearerAuth.description: Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Recommended.

acurisKeyHeader.name: X-Acuris-Key
acurisKeyHeader.description:
API key issued to direct customers who subscribed via Acuris Stripe
Checkout (separate from RapidAPI subscribers). Stripe-issued keys
also work via `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Example:

```
curl -H 'X-Acuris-Key: <your-key>' \
  'https://api.acuris-geo.com/geocode?country=usa&street=Pennsylvania+Ave&hno=1600&city=Washington&state=DC'
```

apiKeyQueryLegacy.name: key
apiKeyQueryLegacy.description:
Legacy query-param auth (`?key=<key>`). Retained for backward
compatibility; prefer header auth — query-string secrets can leak into access logs.

Password.name: key
Password.description:
Legacy API key query parameter (`?key=...`). Prefer `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or
`X-API-Key: <key>` header auth instead.

RateLimitExceeded.description: Too many requests (anonymous limit or WAF/limiter)

pools.description:
The four independently-metered transaction pools. Each pool's `total` is
the greater of the remaining balance and the trial floor (so a granted
account reads N/N rather than N/1000). The `email` and `phone` pools
report a `total` of 0 until they hold transactions.

trial_expires_at.description: UTC trial-window end (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`), or null.

trial_expired.description: True once the trial calendar window has lapsed.

days_left.description: Whole days remaining in the trial window, or null if no/unparseable expiry.

subscription.description: Stripe subscription state for the account's email, or null when none exists.

total.description: Denominator; 0 for the email/phone pools until they are funded.

used_pct.description: Rounded percentage consumed; 0 when total is 0.

recent.description: Up to 15 most recent calls (newest first), summary fields only.

country.description: Data country of the request, when known.

days.description: Daily call counts for the trailing 7 days (oldest first); missing days omitted.

ok.description: Calls with an `ok` result on that day.

calls_7d.description: Total calls across the trailing 7-day window.

api_key.description: The evaluation key. Send it as `X-Acuris-Key: <key>` (or `Authorization: Bearer` / `X-API-Key` / `?key=`) on validation/geocoding calls.

validation_credits.description: Address-validation pool seeded on the key.

geocode_credits.description: Geocode pool seeded on the key.

phone_credits.description: Offline phone-validation pool seeded on the key.

info_url.description: Pricing / info page (UK-specific for a `gbr` country hint).

next_steps.description: Short onboarding note pointing to `/register` for more headroom.

paf_note.description: Present only when the request `country` hint is `gbr` — notes that UK addresses (Royal Mail PAF) are evaluation-only under a dev key.

ValidateBatchRequest.description: Bulk validation payload. An **API key** (header or credentials) is required.

addresses.description:
Up to 200 rows. Each row is either the same `input` shape accepted by
`POST /validate` (a single-line string or an object of address fields),
**or** an object `{"input": <input>, "country": "usa"}` that overrides
`country` for that one row.

country.description:
Default ISO-3 country for every row that does not carry its own
`country` override.

count.description: Number of rows processed (after empty rows are dropped).

results.description: Per-row results in request order; each element is the same body a standalone `POST /validate` returns.

ip.description:
Only on `ip_not_allowed` (403): the source IP address this request
came from, which is not on the key's approved list.

MatchType.description:
Internal/legacy precision tier with the score table below. New clients should
prefer `accuracy_type` for branching.

Unlike `accuracy_type`, this enum is CLOSED — the score table is fixed
and no further values will be added. An `arrival_point` coordinate is
reported here as `rooftop`, because the address is premise-verified
either way; only `accuracy_type` states what the coordinate is.
Score table:
  * `rooftop` → 1.0
  * `parcel_centroid` → 0.9
  * `interpolated` → 0.8
  * `street_level` → 0.6
  * `zip_centroid` → 0.4
  * `city_centroid` → 0.2
  * `no_match` → 0.0
  * `non_deliverable` → 0.0 — the input is a PO Box / Rural Route /
    Postfach etc. and can never resolve to a street address
    (USA/CAN/MEX/DEU/AUT/CHE detection). Returned on the 400 body
    (with `non_deliverable_type`) unless `iso20022: true` opted in to
    a labelled 200.

AccuracyType.description:
What the returned coordinate represents. `null` on `no_match`.

**This is an OPEN set.** New tiers are added as reference data improves.
Clients MUST pass unrecognized values through rather than throwing, and
SHOULD branch on `point_coordinate` rather than on these literals.

A **point coordinate** identifies one address:
  * `rooftop` — a point on the building itself.
  * `arrival_point` — the address's entrance, gate or curb-side access
    point. A point for *this* address, typically a few metres from the
    roof — deliberately not claimed as the building footprint.

Everything else is derived rather than observed — a segment or an area,
not an address:
  * `street_interpolated` — HNO estimated along a street segment polyline
    (SEG cascade) from the position of neighbouring house numbers.
  * `street_centroid` — street confirmed; exact HNO not located.
    **Singapore:** block numbers are not linear along a road and a
    letter-suffixed block (e.g. `700D`) is a separate building with its
    own postcode, so Singapore never returns `street_interpolated`. An
    unconfirmed block (or a street with no block) answers
    `street_centroid` at the street's centre, and
    `standardized.postcode` is left empty unless you supplied a
    postcode that exists on that street — a postcode names one
    building, and another building's postcode is never shown as yours.
  * `landmark_proximity` — India only. The address itself resolved no
    further than its postcode/locality, so the coordinate is that of a
    LANDMARK the caller named in the input ("opp. Swami Samarth Math").
    It is a point on a *neighbouring* place, never the address, and it
    is only ever used when it out-ranks what would otherwise be
    returned. The landmark used is named back to you in
    `landmark_used` (`name`, `matched_from`, `scope`, `source`).
  * `postcode_centroid` — only postcode matched.
  * `locality_centroid` — only city/locality matched.
  * `admin_centroid` — only admin region (state/province) matched.

MatchComponents.description: Which input fields were confirmed by the match.

FailureReason.description:
Why a validation failed to confirm the address (or part of it).

**This is an OPEN set** — new codes are added as matching logic
improves; pass unrecognized values through rather than throwing.
Reasons appear on 404/422 error bodies AND on 200 `partial_match`
responses (stating what the resolved tier could not pin down).
  * `street_not_found` — no street in the candidate set scored highly.
    On a Portugal 200 it appears together with `fell_back_to_locality`
    (`approximate: true`) when the name sent is an estate,
    urbanisation or neighbourhood that is not in the street data but
    whose town we can place: the point is then the town centre.
  * `city_not_matching` — street looked right but the locality did not.
  * `locality_unknown` — we could not even find candidates in the locality.
  * `house_number_interpolated` — house number was interpolated along a street
    segment (`street_interpolated` tier), not confirmed against a rooftop record.
  * `house_number_not_found` — street confirmed but the exact house number is not
    on file.
  * `house_number_unconfirmed` — the house number could not be confirmed
    (`street_centroid` tier partials emit this).
  * `house_number_range_interpolated` — number placed within an official
    numbering range, not a premise row.
  * `street_not_matched` — the street could not be matched; resolution stopped at a
    postcode or locality centroid.
  * `street_unconfirmed` — a street you provided could not be confirmed
    against the matched record.
  * `street_not_found_in_locality` — the street exists but not in the
    stated locality.
  * `postcode_not_matched` — the postcode could not be matched; resolution stopped
    at a locality centroid.
  * `postcode_unconfirmed` / `city_unconfirmed` — the component was echoed
    from input, not confirmed by reference data.
  * `postcode_town_mismatch` — postcode and town point at different places.
  * `postcode_locality_conflict` — postcode and locality conflict (India).
  * `postcode_valid_not_stocked` — the postcode is real but our reference
    data holds no addresses for it (Malaysia; see `postcode_status`).
  * `below_verification_threshold` — the best candidate scored under the
    verification threshold.
  * `no_coordinate_available` — matched a reference row that carries no
    coordinate.
  * `resolved_to_administrative_area_only` — only the admin region (state/province)
    resolved (`admin_centroid` tier).
  * `positioned_at_named_landmark` — coordinate taken from a landmark the
    caller named (India `landmark_proximity`; see `landmark_used`).
  * `non_deliverable_address` — PO Box / Rural Route / Postfach input
    (see `MatchType: non_deliverable`).
  * `search_budget_exhausted` — 404 only. The input did not match
    directly and the recovery search (typo, locality and postcode
    fallbacks) ran out of its per-request time budget (about 10 s)
    before finding a confident answer. This is a no-match, not a
    server error: the address may still exist. Check the input for
    typos or add the postcode, then retry; do not retry the identical
    request in a tight loop.
  * `fuzzy_budget_exceeded` — Sweden (`swe`), `/validate` partial 200s
    and 404s. The street did not match as typed and the search for a
    close real street (typo correction) was cut short by its time
    limit before it finished. It is NOT proof that the street is
    absent: appears together with `street_not_matched` (200) or
    `street_not_found` (404), and the answer stops at a postcode or
    locality centroid. The caller may retry the same request once a
    moment later; a retry usually completes the correction.
  * `street_type_ambiguous` — 404 only (USA). The street NAME exists in
    the given postcode/city, but only with a different street type or
    directional than the one supplied, and more than one real street
    fits (e.g. `12th St N` when both `12th St NE` and `12th St NW` carry
    the house number). We never guess between two real streets: the
    body carries `did_you_mean`, the candidate streets (up to 6) with
    their `city` and `postcode`; resubmit with the intended one.
    Can also appear in a `/geocode-usa` 404 body, when no fallback
    centroid is available for the address.

  * `city_missing` — 404. A street was sent without a city or
    postcode and cannot be placed in a single locality. Sent together
    with another code (e.g. `street_not_found` or
    `street_found_in_multiple_localities`). Seen for several countries
    (e.g. Portugal, Brazil, Spain). Netherlands: also when a postcode
    was sent but is not on file (the `message` then asks for a city
    only); a postcode + house number with no street is answered
    without this code (see `postcode_house_number_ambiguous`).
  * `street_found_in_multiple_localities` — 404. The street name exists
    in more than one locality — of the town you sent, or, when no city
    was sent, of the country. Add the locality or the postcode. When
    no city was sent, `did_you_mean` lists the towns holding the
    street (at most 6).

**Portugal (`country: prt`) only.** The codes below are added to
Portuguese responses on `/validate` and `/geocode` (and their `/v1`
aliases). On a 200 they are appended after the codes listed above,
which keep their meaning and position. On a 404 the first code is the
most specific one.
  * `city_not_found` — 404. The city/town you sent is not a place in
    the Portuguese reference data (often sent with
    `locality_unknown`). Check the spelling or send the postcode.
  * `street_type_mismatch` — 404, sent before `street_not_found`. The
    street name exists in the town only with a different street type
    (e.g. `Rua de Portugal` typed, `Avenida de Portugal` held). See
    `did_you_mean`.
  * `street_particle_mismatch` — 404, as above, when the name differs
    only in its linking particles (`da`, `de`, `do`, `das`, `dos`).
  * `street_spelling_mismatch` — 404, as above, for a close spelling
    of a street of that town.
  * `locality_ambiguous` — 404. A place name sent on its own (no
    street) is a locality in several municipalities and nothing
    coarser; it is never guessed. `did_you_mean` lists the candidates
    with `municipality` and `district`. Sent with `street_missing`.
  * `street_missing` — no street was sent. On a 200 it marks the
    labelled approximate point for a city- or neighbourhood-only
    request (`approximate: true`).
  * `fell_back_to_locality` — 200. A street was sent but could not be
    placed, and the point served is the town/area centre
    (`approximate: true`, `resolved_level`, `resolved_name`), not the
    address. For an estate or neighbourhood name sent with a town it is
    accompanied by `street_not_found`; it can also carry a
    `did_you_mean` hint and its `street_*_mismatch` code.
  * `house_number_not_in_reference` — 200. The street was matched but
    the house number you sent is not in the reference data;
    `nearby_house_numbers` names the closest same-parity numbers that
    are.
  * `house_number_missing` — 200. The street was matched but no house
    number was sent, so only a street-level point is possible.

**Netherlands (`country: nld`), postcode + house number with no street:**
  * `postcode_house_number_ambiguous` — 404, with `street_missing`.
    Several streets hold that house number at that postcode; we never
    guess between them. `did_you_mean` lists them (`street`, `city`,
    `postcode`, `house_number`; at most 6).
  * `house_number_extension_missing` — 200. The number exists at that
    postcode only with a letter (`3A`, `3B`, ...) and none was sent; the
    point is that building, and `did_you_mean` lists the letters.
  * `house_number_not_in_reference` — 200 (`postcode_centroid`). The
    number is not on file at that postcode; `standardized.street` is
    empty (nothing is invented).

NearbyHouseNumbers.description:
**Portugal (`country: prt`) only.** Present on a 200 answer when the
street was matched but the house number you sent is not in the
reference data — the answer is then either street-level
(`street_centroid`) or `street_interpolated` at a point between the
nearest same-parity house numbers (`pin_between`). It lists which
numbers of that street ARE held, on the same side of the street (odd
and even numbers usually face each other). Informational only: it
never changes the coordinate, tier, confidence or `deliverable`. Sent
with reason `house_number_not_in_reference`. Pass unrecognized fields
through.

requested.description: The house number as you sent it.

before.description: The nearest held number below the requested one on the same side, or `null`.

after.description: The nearest held number above the requested one on the same side, or `null`.

pin_between.description: The two held numbers the interpolated point was placed between (both may be the same number, e.g. `41` for a requested `41B`); `null` when the answer is street-level rather than interpolated.

same_parity_available.description: Up to 40 held numbers on the same side nearest to the requested one, in ascending order (letter suffixes such as `2A` included).

total_doors.description: Number of distinct house numbers held for the street.

coordinated_doors.description: How many of those carry their own coordinate.

accuracy.description: The coordinate tier of that house number (e.g. `rooftop`), `null` without a coordinate.

has_coordinates.description: `false` when the number exists in the reference data without its own coordinate (`lat`/`lng`/`accuracy` are then `null`).

ResolvedLevel.description:
**Portugal (`country: prt`) only.** Which kind of place an approximate
point (`approximate: true`) stands for. Open set — pass unknown values
through.
  * `locality` — a locality (village / town).
  * `postal_town` — the town name of the postal address.
  * `municipality` — a municipality (concelho).
  * `district` — a district.
  * `lisbon_parish` — a Lisbon parish or neighbourhood name; the point
    is Lisbon's.

DidYouMeanEntry.description:
One candidate in a 404 `did_you_mean` list — what the input most
likely meant, for you to choose from and resubmit. Never applied
automatically. Which fields are present depends on the case:
  * USA `street_type_ambiguous`: `street`, `city`, `postcode`.
  * Portugal, street not in the town (`street_type_mismatch` /
    `street_particle_mismatch` / `street_spelling_mismatch`):
    `street`, `city`, `doors`, `match`.
  * Portugal, street sent without a city
    (`street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing`):
    `street`, `city`, `municipality`, `doors` (most house numbers
    first, at most 6; see `did_you_mean_truncated`).
  * Portugal, place name only (`locality_ambiguous`): `city`,
    `municipality`, `district`.
  * Other countries' locality/street ambiguities carry their own
    subset (e.g. `street` + `city`, sometimes `state`).

doors.description: Number of addresses (house numbers) held for that street in that locality — a size indicator for ranking.

match.description: How the candidate differs from what was sent: another street type, other linking particles, or a close spelling.

StandardizedAddress.description: Canonical address as stored in the reference database.

city.description:
Spain (`/suggest`): for the officially bilingual municipalities the suggestion prints the Castilian name by default (`Alicante`, `Elche`, `San Sebastián`, `Castellón de la Plana`, `Valencia`); if your query already spells the regional form (`Alacant`, `Elx`, `Donostia`, `València`) that spelling is kept. Postcode and coordinates are the same either way, and submitting the suggestion to `/validate` matches the same address. `/validate` itself echoes the spelling you sent.
Sweden, city + postcode without a street (`/validate`, `/geocode`): the stored spelling of the locality (`Goteborg`, `göteborg` -> `GÖTEBORG`), as on full matches; an English or variant name (`Gothenburg`) is returned in the stored spelling too, and `/validate` lists `City` under `corrections`.

state.description: Present for countries with regions (e.g. USA, CAN, AUS, MYS).

postcode_formatted.description: The postcode as it is written on a letter, in a field of its own, for integrations that look the postcode up elsewhere. Sweden: `412 50` (`postcode` stays `41250`). Where no written form differs, it equals `postcode`. `postcode` itself is unchanged. Returned by `/validate`.

street_type.description: The thoroughfare type as its own element, where the reference data carries it separately: Malaysia (`street_type: "Jalan"`, `street: "Melor 1"`), and Canada / France where the split comes straight from the reference columns (France is type-first — `street_type: "Place"`, `street_name: "de la Comédie"`). NOT emitted for the USA, which would need a USPS-suffix parse, nor for German, Dutch, Danish, Swedish or Swiss addresses, where the type is fused into the word (*Eckenbertstraße*) and splitting it is a morphological judgement rather than a field read.

street_name.description: Canada and France: the bare street name with the type and any directional removed. Companion to `street_type` / `street_suffix`; `street` always holds the full form.

street_suffix.description: Canada: the directional element (N, SW, …) as its own field.

street_id.description: France: the reference data's stable identifier for the thoroughfare.

building_name.description: Hong Kong: the building name from the matched premise. Emitted only when every co-matched row agrees on it — a query resolving to many rows (a tower with hundreds of flats) omits it rather than picking one arbitrarily. Singapore: the building name of the matched block, when it has one (house-number-level matches, and addresses identified by a building or tenant name). It is not part of `formatted_address`.

level_number.description: Denmark (`etage`) and Hong Kong (floor). Same unambiguity rule as `building_name`, and additionally requires a confirmed house number.

unit_identifier.description: Denmark (`dør`), the Netherlands (sub-address) and Hong Kong (flat). Same unambiguity rule as `level_number`.

ine_municipality.description: Spain: the 5-digit INE municipality code of the matched address (leading zeros preserved — always a string).

nis_code.description: Belgium: the NIS municipality code of the matched address.

statistical_sector.description: Belgium: the 9-character Statbel statistical sector of the matched address (the trailing hyphen is part of the code, e.g. `"41002A00-"`). This is the key the Belgian enrichment joins on.

county.description: UK only (`country: "gbr"`). Traditional/postal county, derived from the Royal Mail PAF postcode → county map.

udprn.description: UK only. Royal Mail Unique Delivery Point Reference Number (PAF) — stable identifier for the delivery point.

uprn.description: UK only. Ordnance Survey Unique Property Reference Number. Present when the address matches OS Open UPRN.

unit.description: Sub-building unit, echoed from the caller's input (reference rows carry no unit, so this value is never invented). Rendered into `formatted_address` per country convention (e.g. Canada Post `23-4 Vata Crt`). When the reference data cannot confirm the unit at the matched premise, the response lists `"unit"` in the top-level `unverified_fields` array — the premise match itself still stands. Spain: staircase / floor / door in any common spelling (`ESC.1-PISO 1, PTA.B`, `1º B`, `3º izq`, `bajo`) are normalised to one form, e.g. `Esc. 1, 1º B`; see `unit_verified` / `unit_check`. Latvia: the flat (dzīvoklis) in any common spelling (`Brīvības iela 100 - 5`, `100-5`, `100 dz. 5`, `100 kv. 5`) is returned as the flat number, e.g. `5`, and rendered as `Brīvības iela 100 - 5`; a korpuss (`10k2`, `10 k. 2`) is part of the house number (`10 k-2`), never a unit.

suburb.description: New Zealand. The NZ Post suburb line between street and post town (`68 Rintoul Street / Newtown / Wellington 6021`). Filled from the matched reference row — including when the caller typed only the city. A suburb typed in the city slot is a verified match, never a `City` correction.

district.description: Neighborhood / sub-locality where the country convention carries one (e.g. the Turkish mahalle, Austrian Bezirk sublocality). Enriched from the reference row even when the caller omitted it.

province.description: Italy only. Two-letter province sigla (MI, RM, …) for the mandatory Poste Italiane locality line (`20067 PAULLO MI`).

dependent_street.description: UK only (Royal Mail PAF dependent thoroughfare). The minor road the house number is addressed on (`18 Latium Close, Holywell Hill`); the parent thoroughfare stays in `street`.

dependent_locality.description: UK (Royal Mail PAF): village / dependent locality printed between the thoroughfare and the post town. Malaysia: the Taman / Kampung sub-locality line, printed above the postcode line.

administrative_county.description: UK only. PAF Administrative County (local authority). Present when extended UK fields are enabled; on some postcodes it is the only county held (`county` blank).

welsh.description: UK only, Wales. The Welsh-language form of the SAME delivery point (Royal Mail ships Welsh addresses bilingually): `street`, `city` (post town, e.g. CAERDYDD for CARDIFF) and, where they exist, translated `dependent_locality` / `double_dependent_locality` / `dependent_street`. Present on an English-form match when a Welsh counterpart exists. Typing the Welsh form is a verified match, never a `Street`/`City` correction.

english.description: UK only, Wales. Mirror of `welsh`: the English-language form, present when the matched row is the Welsh one. At most one of `welsh`/`english` appears.

PostcodeAddress.description: One delivery point returned by `/postcode-lookup` (Royal Mail PAF).

post_town.description: The PAF post town; `city` duplicates it for backward compatibility.

address_lines.description: Printable Royal Mail address lines, in order.

administrative_county.description: PAF Administrative County (local authority). On some postcodes (e.g. M1 1AE) it is the only county held — `county` blank. Present when extended UK fields are enabled (on by default).

udprn.description: Royal Mail Unique Delivery Point Reference Number.

uprn.description: Ordnance Survey Unique Property Reference Number.

uprn_match_m.description: Distance in metres between the PAF delivery point and the matched OS Open UPRN coordinate (0.0 is a real and best value). Present when extended UK fields are enabled (on by default).

lat.description: Omitted when no coordinate is available for the delivery point.

lng.description: Omitted when no coordinate is available for the delivery point.

accuracy_type.description: `rooftop` when an address-level coordinate is available, otherwise `postcode` (postcode-unit centroid). Omitted (along with `lat`/`lng`) when the delivery point has no coordinate. Open set — see AccuracyType; do not treat an unrecognized value as a failure.

Suggestion.description:
A ranked near-miss candidate returned on `/validate` (score ≥ 0.5, below
the correction threshold). Appears in `suggestions[]` on 404 no-match
responses and on 200 `partial_match` responses where the street could not
be matched — offering the closest real streets in the caller's
postcode/locality. Not normally present on verified/corrected successes.

SuggestItem.description:
One autocomplete suggestion from `/suggest`. Carries the
StandardizedAddress fields (flat, not nested) plus the additions below.
UK identifiers (`udprn`, `uprn`, `county`) are **never** present on
suggestions — obtain them by submitting the chosen suggestion to
`/validate` or via `/postcode-lookup`.

lat.description: Omitted when the reference row carries no coordinate — never invented.

lng.description: Omitted when the reference row carries no coordinate — never invented.

count.description: Number of reference premises merged into this row; present when more than one. Germany (`deu`): when the query carries no house number, the printed `formatted_address` of such a row is street-level (street, postcode and town, no house number) once the street-level label is enabled; `house_number` and the coordinates (v=1) are those of one representative premise, and `GET /suggest/expand` lists the street's premises, up to 50 per page (`offset` selects the next page; `has_more` / `next_offset` in the answer), up to 400 per street.

locality.description: Secondary locality, for countries whose reference data carries no postal code column (e.g. IRL).

building_name.description: UK postcode-mode: labels each delivery point at the postcode.

organisation_name.description: UK postcode-mode: organisation at the delivery point.

department.description: UK postcode-mode: department within the organisation.

jpn_zip.description: JPN: feed back as the `zip` parameter for the stage-2 banchi-gō lookup.

jpn_oaza_norm.description: JPN: feed back as the `oaza` parameter for the stage-2 lookup.
