jpn_chome.description: JPN: feed back as the `chome` parameter for the stage-2 lookup.

building.description: SGP: the building name of the suggested premise. When the query matched a building name, this is the name that was matched (a building known under more than one name shows the one you typed). Never part of `formatted_address`. Also returned on `v=2` list rows.

tenant.description: SGP: when the query matched the name of a business at the premise (e.g. `mcdonalds`), that name as listed. A business with several outlets returns up to five of its premises, each with its own `building`. Never part of `formatted_address`. Also returned on `v=2` list rows.

AlternativeMatch.description:
**Reserved — not currently emitted** (disabled in production pending a
street-leading index). Planned behaviour: same street + same house
number in a different state, on USA / CAN `verified` (exact) matches
only, bounded to 5 rows.

score.description: Always 1.0 — these are exact DB matches in a different state.

country.description:
ISO-3 country code, lowercase. Any country in the acceptance set
(~223 live today — see **Country codes** in the API description)
validates and returns the best tier its reference data supports;
inspect `accuracy_type`. Highest-precision coverage includes `usa`,
`can`, `gbr` (served from the PAF host — see Servers), `deu`,
`aut`, `che`, `fra`, `esp`, `bel`, `nld`, `dnk`, `fin`, `swe`,
`nor`, `ita`, `jpn`, `sgp`, among others. `country_code` and
`countryCode` are accepted as aliases of this field.

input.description:
Single-line address string **or** object with `street`, `house_number`, `city`,
`postcode`, `state`, `unit`, `floor`, `po_box`, `sublocality`, etc.

**`sublocality`** is the administrative tier *below* the city — Vietnamese
phường/xã, Indonesian kelurahan, Thai tambon, Philippine barangay. Send it in
its own field rather than folding it into `city`, which carries the tier the
reference data keys on (in Vietnam, the district). Your own word for the tier is
accepted as an alias: `ward`, `sub_locality`, `sub_district`, `subdistrict`,
`kelurahan`, `barangay`, `tambon`.

It **narrows, it never vetoes**: a sub-locality we do not hold, or one written
in a naming scheme newer than the reference data, returns exactly the result the
same request returns without it. So it is always safe to send.

Wired for **`vnm`** today, where it separates addresses that share a district,
street and house number across different wards. Other countries accept and
ignore it until their reference data carries the tier.

key.description: API key in the body (legacy). Header auth is preferred.

db_version.description: Ignored. Same reference DB as geocode (ref_dbs.json).

ValidateResponse.description:
Successful validation **or** centroid-fallback. The canonical form
**always lives in `standardized`**. When value-changing corrections were
applied, the response carries `status: "corrected"` with a
human-readable `corrections` list, and `standardized` holds the
corrected canonical form. When neither was attainable but SEG produced a
centroid, the response carries `partial_match: true` with `lat`/`lng`
set; `standardized` then echoes the caller's input for every component
that could not be verified — only the components confirmed in
`match_components` are reference data. All responses carry the
match-quality contract (`match_type`, `match_score`, `match_components`,
`input_corrected`).

corrected.description: Reserved legacy key — not emitted. The corrected canonical form is returned in `standardized` (with `status: "corrected"` and the `corrections` list); read that instead.

status.description: `verified` = the street and house number matched exactly; postcode/locality repairs derived unambiguously from the matched premise may still appear in `corrections` (with `postcode_corrected: true` and `confidence_level` capped at `medium`) without demoting status. `corrected` = the street or city itself required a value-changing correction (fuzzy match above the 0.85 similarity threshold, or standardized fields). Omitted (with `partial_match: true`) when the address could not be verified. Standardization is never a correction: for a city-state (Singapore, Monaco) the city implied by the country — filled in when you omit it, or typed as an alias such as `SG` / `Republic of Singapore` — does not appear in `corrections` and does not make the status `corrected`; nor do Singapore street-type abbreviations (`Jln` = Jalan, `Bt` = Bukit, `Ave`, `Cres`, `Cl`, …). A genuinely different city or a misspelt street is still reported.

confidence.description: 1.0 for a `verified` match; the similarity score (0.85–1.0) for a `corrected` match — but capped at match_score (0.2–0.6) whenever a street or house number you PROVIDED could not be confirmed against the matched record (e.g. the match fell back to a different street, or the house number is not on file). confidence_level is demoted to `low` in the same cases.

confidence_level.description: Plain confidence grade for bulk-CSV workflows. `high` = confirmed exact, `medium` = confirmed with safe corrections, `low` = partial/approximate (e.g. house number not found, or a locality/admin-area centroid only), `none` = no match.

corrections.description: Human-readable list of corrected input fields (e.g. `["Postal code", "City"]`). `"House number"` appears when the house number in the answer differs from the one you sent because the building was renumbered (Latvia, see `former_address`).

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added. Emitted on matches and street-tier partials; omitted on postcode/locality/admin-centroid fallbacks.

reasons.description: Present on `partial_match` responses: why full verification failed (e.g. `street_not_matched`, `house_number_unconfirmed`). The same codes appear on 404/422 error bodies.

provided_components.description: **Always returned.** Echoes which components the caller actually supplied (non-empty after parsing), keyed identically to `match_components` (`house_number`, `street`, `city`, `zip`, `state`). Pair it with `match_components` field-by-field to tell "not provided" apart from "provided but not matched".

partial_match.description:
`true` when the address could not be fully verified but a coordinate was still
produced — at street level (`street_interpolated` / `street_centroid`: street
confirmed, house number not) or via the SEG cascade (postcode / locality / admin
centroid). Absent or `false` on full verified/corrected matches. The response
still carries `standardized`, but it echoes the caller's input for every
component that could not be verified (only the components confirmed in
`match_components` are reference data) — treat `lat`/`lng` as the only
trustworthy output, and check `reasons` for what could not be pinned down.

nearby_house_numbers.description: Portugal only, optional. The street was matched but the house number you sent is not in the reference data (`street_centroid`, or `street_interpolated` between the nearest same-parity numbers with `confidence` 0.8 and `deliverable: false`); names the nearest numbers that are held. Sent with reason `house_number_not_in_reference`.

street_postcodes.description: Netherlands only, optional. Present only on STREET-LEVEL answers (`accuracy_type` `street_centroid`, `street_segment_centroid` or `street_interpolated`): the postcodes the matched street covers, each with its house-number range. Sorted by `house_number_from`, then `postcode`; at most 50 entries (see `street_postcodes_total` and `street_postcodes_truncated`). Ranges count numeric house numbers only; addresses whose number carries letters are not counted. Absent on rooftop and other house-number-level answers.

parity.description: Which side(s) of the street the postcode covers within that range.

street_postcodes_total.description: With `street_postcodes`, how many postcodes the street covers (not capped).

street_postcodes_truncated.description: With `street_postcodes`, `true` when the street covers more postcodes than are listed.

postcode_range.description: Netherlands only, optional. Sent with `street_postcodes` when the street covers MORE THAN ONE postcode: the lowest and highest postcode over the whole street (an outer bound, not a continuous run; `street_postcodes` lists the exact ones). In that case `standardized.postcode` carries `text` instead of a single postcode and `standardized.formatted_address` prints it. Check for this field before treating `standardized.postcode` as one postcode.

approximate.description: Portugal only, optional. `true` when the point is a town / area centre standing in for the address: a city- or neighbourhood-only request (reason `street_missing`), a street that could not be placed (reason `fell_back_to_locality`), or an estate / urbanisation name sent with a town we can place (reasons `street_not_found` + `fell_back_to_locality`). `accuracy_type` is then `locality_centroid` or `admin_centroid` and `confidence` is 0.4 or lower. Absent otherwise.

resolved_level.description: Portugal only, with `approximate: true`: which kind of place the point stands for (`locality`, `postal_town`, `municipality`, `district`, `lisbon_parish`).

resolved_name.description: Portugal only, with `approximate: true`: the name of that place as spelled in the reference data (e.g. `Cascais`; `Lisboa` for a Lisbon neighbourhood).

enrichment.description:
Free geographic enrichment, attached automatically (no extra
charge, no request parameter) for eighteen countries — USA,
Canada, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, United Kingdom,
Belgium, Spain, Portugal, Ireland, Netherlands, Finland, Sweden,
Luxembourg, Japan, Singapore and Hong Kong — whenever the result
is precise
enough for a small-area lookup to be trustworthy (gates below).
Omitted otherwise — never null, never an empty object. Fields whose
geography does not apply to the point are likewise omitted, never
null. Sub-fields are country-specific; every layer is public
government data.

**When it appears**

- USA, Canada, Germany, Austria, Switzerland and the France admin
  fields need a street-accurate coordinate (`rooftop`,
  `arrival_point`, `street_interpolated` or `street_centroid` —
  never a postcode/locality/admin centroid, where the point could
  fall in the wrong small area).
- The France `building` block and the whole UK block need a
  premise-level match (`rooftop` / `arrival_point`). The UK block
  is keyed on the matched address's `uprn` (ONS National Statistics
  UPRN Lookup). Great Britain only — Northern Ireland (BT
  postcodes) carries no block because NI statistical geography is
  separately licensed.
- Finland and the Netherlands are keyed on the validated postcode;
  the block describes the whole postal area (see its `scope`
  field), not the individual household.
- Japan derives the 500 m JIS X 0410 mesh cell from the
  coordinate.
- Singapore joins on the standardized block number + street; HDB
  blocks only, so a miss on private housing is normal.
- Belgium is keyed on the matched row's 9-character Statbel
  statistical sector (also emitted as `statistical_sector`); a
  Belgian postcode spans several sectors, so a postcode-grain join
  would attribute one sector's figures to all of them.
- Spain resolves the 10-digit census section (CUSEC) from the INE
  Callejero — municipality + street + house-number range + parity —
  and falls back to municipality level when no range covers the
  number. The block's `scope` says which tier answered
  (`census_section` or `municipality`); the parity filter is
  load-bearing and refuses rather than assigning the wrong side of
  the street.
- Portugal, Ireland, Sweden, Luxembourg and Hong Kong are
  point-in-polygon on the returned coordinate, each returning a
  `statistical_area` block whose `code` is that country's finest
  published unit: Portugal BGRI subsecção (11 chars, block-level),
  Ireland CSO Small Area (2022), Sweden DeSO, Luxembourg commune
  (LAU2), Hong Kong Small Subunit Group.
- Three Irish Small Areas genuinely overlap (slivers of 38–433 m²
  from 20 m generalisation). A point inside one is reported as
  ambiguous rather than silently resolved — picking the smallest
  area would cross an electoral-district boundary in Carlow.

Enrichment can accompany `partial_match: true` when the inferred
coordinate still reaches a qualifying tier (e.g.
`street_centroid`); postcode-, locality- and admin-centroid
fallbacks never carry it.

Statistical layers respect the publisher's disclosure control:
withheld values are absent from the block — an absent value is not
a zero (Swiss hectare grid, Dutch PC6, Japanese age bands) — and
German Zensus grid counts are Cell-Key perturbed. Each such block
says so in its `note`.

census_tract.description: USA: 11-digit census tract GEOID. Canada: CTUID (urban areas only).

cbsa.description: USA: Core-Based Statistical Area (metro/micro). Omitted (not null) outside any CBSA.

dissemination_area.description: Canada: 8-digit Dissemination Area UID (province + census division + DA).

cma_ca.description: Canada: Census Metropolitan Area / Census Agglomeration. Omitted outside both.

gemeinde_type.description: Germany: municipality kind (Stadt, Gemeinde, Kreisfreie Stadt, …).

zaehlsprengel.description: Austria: census enumeration district (smallest census unit).

kanton.description: Switzerland: canton — also the Nationalrat electoral constituency.

grossregion.description: Switzerland: major region = Swiss NUTS-2 unit.

sprachgebiet.description: Switzerland: official language region — which language to address this customer in.

gemeindetyp.description: Switzerland: BFS municipality typology (9 classes); `class` is the 3-fold split.

iris.description: France: INSEE IRIS statistical district (metropolitan France).

building.description: France, premise-level matches only: the IGN BD TOPO building the coordinate falls on (or the nearest within 8 m). `coord_verified` is true when the point is inside or ≤ 2 m from the footprint. `sub_unit_expected` is true when the building is multi-dwelling and the caller supplied no apartment/unit — the address is probably incomplete.

output_area.description: UK: 2021 Output Area code — finest ONS tier; output areas have no name.

lsoa.description: UK: Lower layer Super Output Area.

msoa.description: UK: Middle layer Super Output Area.

demographics.description: Germany: Zensus 2022 100 m grid — grid_cell, population, avg_age, avg_household_size, avg_net_rent_per_sqm, owner_occupier_pct, vacancy_pct, foreign_national_pct; small counts are Cell-Key perturbed (approximate). Switzerland: BFS STATPOP 100 m hectare grid — hectare_cell, population, buildings, dwellings; withheld cells are absent (an absent value is not a zero). Always carries `note` and `source`.

economy.description: Switzerland: BFS STATENT hectare-grid workplace stats — hectare_cell, workplaces, employees_fte, note, source.

postal_area.description: Finland: Statistics Finland PAAVO statistics for the whole postal area (`scope: postal_area`) — names (fi/sv), municipality_code, area_km2, centroid, population + age bands, mean/median incomes (personal and household), employment, jobs_total, households by type/tenure, dwellings, avg_dwelling_area_m2, summer_cottages. CC BY 4.0; `source` inside the block.

postcode_area.description: Netherlands: CBS Kerncijfers for the six-character postcode (`scope: postcode6_area`) — inhabitants + age bands, households by type, dwellings, avg_home_value_eur, pct_owner_occupied, pct_rented, persons_on_benefits, avg_gas_m3, avg_electricity_kwh. CBS-suppressed cells are absent, never 0.

mesh_area.description: Japan: 2020 Population Census on the 500 m JIS X 0410 mesh (`scope: mesh_500m`) — mesh_code, pop_total, pop_male, pop_female, pop_0_14, pop_15_64, pop_65_plus, households. Withheld age bands are absent.

hdb_block.description: Singapore: HDB Property Information for the matched block (`scope: hdb_block`) — bldg_contract_town, max_floor_lvl, year_completed, residential / commercial / market_hawker / multistorey_carpark / precinct_pavilion / miscellaneous flags, total_dwelling_units and the full unit mix (units_1room … units_studio, rental_1room … rental_other). HDB blocks only — private housing has no block.

statistical_sector_area.description: Belgium: Statbel figures for the address's statistical sector (`scope: statistical_sector`) — municipality NIS code and names (NL/FR), sector names, population, density, area, and median / mean taxable income with its reference year.

census_section_area.description: Spain: INE figures for the census section resolved from the Callejero (`scope: census_section`), or for the municipality when no house-number range covers the address (`scope: municipality`). Carries `cusec` (10-digit section code) when section-level, plus population, age structure, nationality mix, household size, education breakdown and the household income series (net / gross, per person and per household). `income_top_coded: true` marks INE's censoring ceiling. Withheld figures are absent, not zero.

statistical_area.description: Portugal, Ireland, Sweden, Luxembourg and Hong Kong: the country's finest published statistical unit, resolved by point-in-polygon on the returned coordinate (`scope: statistical_area`). `code` is the official identifier — Portugal BGRI subsecção (11 chars, block-level, with its dt / dtmn / dicofre components and the Censos 2021 building, dwelling, household and population counts); Ireland CSO Small Area 2022 (~100 dwellings, with SAPS age, tenure, education and commuting); Sweden DeSO (with its RegSO, kommun and län codes); Luxembourg commune LAU2 (with canton, district and STATEC census figures); Hong Kong Small Subunit Group (2021 Census, names in English and Traditional Chinese). ⚠️ Ireland only: three Small Areas overlap in slivers of 38–433 m². A point inside one is reported ambiguous rather than resolved to a single area.

source.description: Attribution for the country's primary layer (present for USA, Canada, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France and the UK). Sub-blocks (`demographics`, `economy`, `building`) and the whole-block countries (`postal_area`, `postcode_area`, `mesh_area`, `hdb_block`) carry their own `source` inside the block — there is no top-level `source` for Finland, the Netherlands, Japan or Singapore. Reproduce these strings where the underlying data licence requires attribution (CC BY 4.0, Etalab 2.0, dl-de/by-2-0, Statistics Canada Open Licence, Singapore Open Data Licence).

match_type_legacy.description: Retained for backward compatibility. New clients should use `match_type`.

match_score_legacy.description: Retained for backward compatibility. Human-readable label (e.g. `"Perfect match"`, `"Partial match (street only)"`).

suggestions.description: Ranked near-miss candidates (score ≥ 0.5, below the correction threshold). Appears on 200 `partial_match` responses where the street could not be matched — the closest real streets in the caller's postcode/locality (up to 3 items) — and on 404 no-match responses. Not normally present on verified/corrected successes.

alternative_matches.description: Reserved — not currently emitted (disabled pending an index). Planned behaviour: same street + house number in a different state, USA / CAN `verified` matches, up to 5 items.

arrival_point.description: Entrance / access coordinate (arrival point) of the matched premise, returned beside the served coordinate on house-number-level matches when the reference row carries one. With `accuracy_type: rooftop` this is the door/curb point of the same address (useful for delivery and navigation); with `accuracy_type: arrival_point` it simply equals `lat`/`lng`. Omitted when the match is not premise-level or no arrival point is on file — never null.

landmark_used.description: Present ONLY with `accuracy_type: landmark_proximity` (India). The address itself resolved no further than its postcode/locality, so the served coordinate was taken from a landmark named in the input. This block says which one, so the substitution is never silent: `name` is the stored name of the place we used, `matched_from` is the caller's own words that matched it, `scope` is the evidence that identified it uniquely (`pin_exact`, `pin_contains`, `locality_exact`, `locality_contains`), and `source` is the data attribution. Omitted on every other tier — never null.

matched_from.description: The landmark text as the caller wrote it.

house_number_not_found.description: The house number you sent is not on file for the matched street — either flagged by the matcher itself, or caught by the input-vs-returned comparison (a fallback row carried a different number). standardized keeps YOUR house number in this case; match tier is capped at street_level.

deliverable.description: `true` only when the address verified confidently against the reference data — `confidence_level` high or medium AND not a partial/centroid fallback AND a premise is identified (a house number you supplied, or a UK premise anchor / named building). This is the same threshold the on-page widget uses for its "valid & deliverable" verdict, so API and UI never disagree. Reflects confirmation against our authoritative reference data; it is not a CASS/DPV-certified delivery guarantee.

hno_range_verified.description: The house number was confirmed against an official numbering RANGE for the street, not an individual premise row (interpolated-tier evidence, e.g. Brazil's official street ranges). Caps `confidence_level` at `medium` — `high` is reserved for premise-level verification.

parsed.description: Always returned. For single-line `input`: the parser's field breakdown (informational echo; lowercase). For fielded input: an echo of the supplied fields. Keys include `street`, `house_number`, `city`, `postcode`, `state`, `sublocality`, `unit`, `floor`, `po_box`, `country`. Useful for debugging why a free-form string matched the way it did. Informational only, not a stable contract: formats can change between releases (for Spain, `floor` carries a normalised code such as `1`, `BJ` for ground floor or `-1` for a basement). Use `standardized` for anything you store or display.

match_details.description: Per-component flags from the DB lookup — keys `street`, `house_number`, `city`, `postcode` (not `zip`), `state` (when applicable), plus a duplicated `postcode_corrected` boolean. Unlike `match_components` — which scores only what the caller provided — `match_details` reports what the matched row confirmed, so the two may legitimately differ. Absent on SEG centroid-fallback responses (still present on street-tier partials).

unverified_fields.description: Components echoed from the caller's input that reference data could NOT confirm (e.g. `["unit"]` — reference rows carry no unit data). The match itself still stands; treat the listed components as unverified input, not reference data.

unit_verified.description: Spain, Latvia and Singapore only. Present and `true` only when the sub-building unit you sent is listed for the matched building. Spain: staircase / floor / door (e.g. `Esc. 1, 1º B`) listed for the matched portal in a 2017 building-unit snapshot. It means "listed in that snapshot", nothing more: the snapshot is not current and covers multi-unit portals only. Latvia: the flat is in the State Address Register's dwelling list for the matched building. Singapore: the `#floor-unit` you sent (e.g. `#12-1415`, `#B2-19`) is in the unit list of the matched block; the floor-unit may be written with or without the `#` marker. Absent when no unit was sent, when no house number was sent, and in every other country. It never changes `confidence`.

former_address.description: Latvia only. The address you sent is a FORMER address of the matched building in the State Address Register: the street was renamed, the building was renumbered, or a named property got a street address (or the reverse). `standardized` holds the current address. The change is disclosed in `corrections` (`Street`, `House number`) and `status` is `corrected`. Absent when the address you sent is current, and in every other country.

street.description: The former street, or the former property name.

house_number.description: The former house number (empty for a former property name).

city.description: City or village at the time (may be empty).

parish.description: Parish (pagasts) at the time (may be empty).

postcode.description: Postcode at the time (empty for records older than 2003).

valid_until.description: Last day the former address was in force, when recorded.

change.description: What changed between the former and the current address.

tenant_name_matched.description: Singapore only. The tenant or shop name (e.g. `MCDONALD'S`) that text in your input matched at the returned building, exactly as we hold it. The name is not part of the standardized address and never enters `formatted_address`. Absent when your input carried no tenant name.

building_name_matched.description: Singapore only. The building name that text in your input matched at the returned building, when it differs from `standardized.building_name` (another name the same building is known by). Absent when it is the same name or none was matched.

unit_check.description: Spain, Latvia and Singapore only. What the reference unit list could say about the unit you sent. `verified`: listed at this building. `not_in_list`: the building has a unit list and yours is not in it. `no_data`: no usable list for this building (Spain: portal not covered, ambiguous match, or a single-dwelling portal; Latvia: checked against the State Address Register's dwelling list, and `no_data` when the building has no registered dwellings, as for single-dwelling houses, or the match is ambiguous; Singapore: the unit lists are not complete for every building, so `not_in_list` means the unit should be re-checked with the addressee, never that it does not exist, and `no_data` is returned when the building has no usable list or the list cannot rule the unit out). For `not_in_list` and `no_data` the response also lists `"unit"` in `unverified_fields`; the address match and `confidence` are unchanged and your unit is still echoed in `standardized.unit`. A unit the parser cannot read at all (`pta`, `Oficina 3`, `Bloque`) also answers `no_data`. Absent when no unit was sent.

postcode_unverified.description: The postcode was echoed from the caller, never read from a reference row.

locality_from_postcode.description: The city was derived from the postcode rather than typed by the caller.

city_backfilled_from_postcode.description: No city was sent; the one in `standardized.city` was derived from the postcode (or, Netherlands, from the postcode + house number). A disclosure, not a correction. Absent otherwise.

street_backfilled_from_postcode.description: Netherlands: no street was sent; the street in `standardized.street` is the one that holds the house number at the postcode sent. A disclosure, not a correction (`corrections` stays empty). Absent otherwise.

matched_via_alias.description: The locality matched through a recognised alias (e.g. a USPS alternate city name) rather than the primary name. `usps_city` and `locality_note` disclose the specifics where applicable.

usps_city.description: USA: the USPS-preferred city name when it differs from the input.

locality_note.description: Human-readable note on how the locality was matched (alias / municipality disclosure).

city_mismatch_ignored.description: The typed city disagreed with the matched row but was overridden by stronger evidence (street + postcode); disclosed rather than silently dropped.

postcode_supplied.description: Postcode-repair forensics — the postcode the caller sent. Also present on its own (without `postcode_suggested`) when the reasons carry `postcode_not_matched` (Sweden): the typed postcode matched nothing in the reference data, so it is returned here as typed and `standardized.postcode` is null.

postcode_suggested.description: Postcode-repair forensics — the reference postcode for the matched premise, when it differs from `postcode_supplied`.

postcode_incoherent.description: `true` when the supplied postcode does not fit the matched street/locality at all (rather than being a near-miss).

postcode_status.description: Malaysia: whether the postcode is held with addresses (`stocked`), real but with no addresses on file (`valid_not_stocked` — see the matching reason code), or unknown. Companion fields `postcode_place` / `postcode_state` name the postal place when known.

accuracy_label.description: Human-readable form of the served tier (e.g. `"postcode centroid"`). Display-only; branch on `accuracy_type` / `point_coordinate`.

non_deliverable_type.description: Classification of non-deliverable input (e.g. `po_box`). Appears on the 400 rejection body, or on the 200 body under `iso20022: true`.

uprn_match_m.description: UK only. Distance in metres between the Royal Mail PAF delivery point and the matched OS Open UPRN coordinate (0.0 is a real and best value). Present when extended UK fields are enabled (on by default).

GeocodeErrorBody.description:
Error body for 404 on the legacy `/geocode-usa` and `/geocode-uk` shorthand
endpoints. Carries the match-quality contract so clients can key on the same
fields regardless of success or failure. Unlike `ValidateErrorBody`, geocode
errors do not include `suggestions`. A `/geocode-usa` 404 may carry
`reasons` and `did_you_mean` when the engine can name the ambiguity —
e.g. `reasons: ["street_type_ambiguous"]` with candidate streets (see
`FailureReason` and `ValidateErrorBody.did_you_mean`). The no-match body omits
`accuracy_type`, so it is not in the required list. For `/geocode` and
`/v1/geocode`, see `ForwardGeocodeErrorBody` instead — the AV match-quality
contract was retired from those two routes.

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added. Optional but always emitted on a match.

reasons.description: `/geocode-usa` only, when present — e.g. `street_type_ambiguous` (with `did_you_mean`). Absent on most geocode misses.

did_you_mean.description: Candidates the caller may have meant (e.g. for `street_type_ambiguous`) — see `ValidateErrorBody.did_you_mean`.

ForwardGeocodeErrorBody.description:
Error body for 404 (no match) and 422 (uninterpretable input) on `/geocode`
and `/v1/geocode`. Deliberately not `GeocodeErrorBody`'s shape — no
`match_type`, `match_score`, `match_components`, or `input_corrected`. A miss
states the fact plainly and nothing else.

**Portugal (`country: prt`):** a 404 may also carry `reasons` (why the
lookup missed), `did_you_mean` (what the input most likely meant —
never applied automatically) and `did_you_mean_truncated`, and
`message` is then a specific English sentence, e.g. `Street 'Rua de
Portugal' not found in Estoril; did you mean Avenida de Portugal?`.
These keys are optional and additive: they are absent for other
countries and whenever nothing more specific than "not found" is
known.

message.description: Human-readable English text. Generic (`Address not found`) unless a specific explanation is available (Portugal). For display only — branch on `reasons`, never on this text.

reasons.description: Portugal only: machine-readable classification of the miss, most specific first — see `FailureReason` (e.g. `city_not_found`, `street_not_found`, `street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing`, `locality_ambiguous` + `street_missing`, or `street_type_mismatch` + `street_not_found`). Absent when nothing more specific is known.

did_you_mean.description: Portugal: up to 6 candidates the input most likely meant, for you to choose from and resubmit — never applied automatically. See `DidYouMeanEntry` for which fields each case carries.

did_you_mean_truncated.description: `true` when more candidates exist than `did_you_mean` lists (a street sent without a city that exists in more than 6 towns; the 6 with the most house numbers are listed). Absent otherwise.

locality_count.description: A street sent WITHOUT a city that exists in several places: how many places it was found in. `message` then reads `That street exists in several places (538). Please specify a city or postcode.` and `reasons` carries `street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing`. Not sent for Spain, nor when the count could not be established.

locality_count_exact.description: With `locality_count`: `true` when exact, `false` when a lower bound (`message` reads `N or more`).

ValidateErrorBody.description:
Error body for 404 and 422 on `/validate` — and for the 400 returned on
non-deliverable input (PO Box etc.), which carries `match_type:
"non_deliverable"` plus `non_deliverable_type`. Carries the
match-quality contract so clients can key on the same fields regardless
of success or failure.

message.description: Human-readable English text; for display only, branch on `error` and `reasons`. Where we can say more it is specific: `That street exists in several places (538). Please specify a city or postcode.` for a street sent with no city (400 `Missing required field: city`, or the 404 for 2-6 places; Netherlands: `Please specify a city.` when the postcode sent is not on file); what to send for `Country is required` (400) and for `Input must be a single-line string or a fielded/JSON object` (422).

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added. Optional but always emitted on a match.

reasons.description: One or more classifications of why the match failed. (The same codes also appear on 200 `partial_match` responses — see `ValidateResponse.reasons`.)

did_you_mean.description: 404 only, when present: candidate addresses the input most likely meant, for the caller to choose from and resubmit — never applied automatically. Sent with `reasons: ["street_type_ambiguous"]` (USA: the same street name with different types/directionals, each entry `street` + `city` + `postcode`) and on some locality/street ambiguities in other countries. Portugal: also when the street is not in the town you sent but a street of that town differs only in type, linking particles or spelling (`street_type_mismatch` / `street_particle_mismatch` / `street_spelling_mismatch`, each entry `street` + `city` + `doors` + `match`), when a street sent without a city exists in several towns (`street`, `city`, `municipality`, `doors`), and when a place name sent on its own is ambiguous (`locality_ambiguous`: `city`, `municipality`, `district`). Sent alongside `suggestions` (which are unchanged). Netherlands: when several streets hold the house number at the postcode sent (`postcode_house_number_ambiguous`), each entry is `street` + `city` + `postcode` + `house_number`; the same shape lists the letters on a 200 with `house_number_extension_missing`. See `DidYouMeanEntry`. Pass unrecognized entry fields through.

house_number.description: Netherlands — the house number incl. its letter (`12A`).

doors.description: Portugal — number of addresses (house numbers) held for that street in that locality.

match.description: Portugal — how the candidate differs from what was sent: another street type, other linking particles, or a close spelling.

did_you_mean_truncated.description: Portugal, 404 only: `true` when more candidates exist than `did_you_mean` lists (a street sent without a city that exists in more than 6 towns). Absent otherwise.

locality_count.description: A street sent WITHOUT a city that exists in several places: how many places (localities) it was found in. Sent with `reasons` `street_found_in_multiple_localities` + `city_missing` on the 400 `Missing required field: city` (7 or more places) and on the 404 for 2-6 places. Not sent for Spain, nor when the count could not be established.

locality_count_exact.description: With `locality_count`: `true` when the count is exact, `false` when it is a lower bound (the `message` then reads `N or more`).

received.description: Sent on the 400 `Country is required` and the 422 `Input must be a single-line string or a fielded/JSON object`, so an integrator can see how the request arrived. Names and types only, never values; authentication keys are never listed.

input_type.description: 422 only. The type of `input` as we received it (`null` when absent).

param_names.description: Parameter names that arrived next to the reserved ones (at most 20).

non_deliverable_type.description: 400 non-deliverable rejections only — what the input is (e.g. `po_box`).

suggestions.description: Top-3 near-miss candidates scoring ≥ 0.5 but below the 0.85 fuzzy threshold (404 only).

parsed.description: If present, the parser's best-effort field breakdown of the input.

Iso20022Block.description:
**Opt-in / beta.** Present only when the request set `"iso20022": true` (body)
or `?iso20022=1`. Maps the validation result onto Swift **CBPR+** postal-address
shapes and adds an explicit truth verdict — what we could structure, what we can
actively refute, and what we simply could not confirm. `Ctry` + `TwnNm` are the
only mandatory ISO elements: without both, no legal shape exists and
`cannot_structure` is `true`. Fields not resolved are omitted (not invented).

structured.description: Fully structured CBPR+ address (component tags only, no `AdrLine`). `null` when the mandatory `Ctry`+`TwnNm` pair is absent. Tags: `Ctry` (ISO alpha-2), `TwnNm`, and — when resolved — `StrtNm`, `BldgNb`, `PstCd`, `CtrySubDvsn`, `Flr`, `Room`, `PstBx`.

hybrid.description: Hybrid shape for callers that must pass the payee's own street rendering through unaltered (EPC153-22): `Ctry`+`TwnNm` (+ `PstCd`, `CtrySubDvsn`) structured, with the unresolved remainder preserved verbatim in `AdrLine[]`. `null` when mandatory elements are absent.

cannot_structure.description: `true` when no legal CBPR+ shape could be emitted (missing Ctry or TwnNm).

assertions.description: Tri-state truth claims. `null` means "not tested" — deliberately distinct from `false` ("tested and wrong").

refutation.description: Hard negatives only — claims we can defend as "this address is wrong" (e.g. `town_not_in_country`, `postcode_town_mismatch`). A street we simply cannot find is NEVER a refutation.

unresolved.description: Coverage gaps — "we could not confirm" (e.g. `street_unconfirmed`), never "this is false".

suggested.description: Advisory-only reference values the engine deliberately did NOT write into the emitted tags (the payee address passes through unaltered). e.g. `PstCd` when the caller's postcode was incoherent. `null` when there is nothing to suggest.

InteractiveElementStatus.description: Per-element input/result status for one interactive result (named-key JSON rendering of the AD 20-position EIS/ERS strings). Keys present depend on the candidate; `number.extended` = `D` marks a house number interpolated from a range.

result_percentage.description: Similarity of the candidate to the parsed input (0–100); the sort key.

standardized.description: Single-line display rendering of the candidate.

range.description: Valid house-number range for an unexpanded tail entry.

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added. Optional but always emitted on a match.

InteractiveEnvelope.description:
**Opt-in / beta.** Returned by `POST /validate` when the request set
`"mode": "interactive"` (AD-parity resolver). Instead of a single batch verdict,
it returns a ranked pick-list of candidate addresses / valid house-number ranges,
keyed on an AD `ProcessStatus` lattice. A **unique** definite match returns
`count: 1` with the same result as batch — no pick-list is fabricated. Billed
identically to a batch validation (1 transaction). Request-only fields: `mode`
(`batch` | `interactive`), a **fielded** `input` object (required — a string
input is rejected), `max_results` (1–100, default 20), `ranges_to_expand`
(`none` | `all` | `only_with_valid_items`), `flexible_range_expansion` (bool).

mode_used.description: The resolver path actually taken (`parse` = degraded).

process_status.description: AD ProcessStatus lattice value — `V4`..`V1` (verified), `C4`..`C1` (corrected), `I4`..`I1` (incomplete/suggestions), `N2` (reference DB unavailable), `N1` (country unsupported).

mailability.description: Mailability score 0–5, derived from `process_status`. Emitted for compatibility; do not branch on it.

count_overflow.description: `true` when more matches existed than `max_results` allowed.

resolution.description: ARC-equivalent — why resolution stopped and how to fix it (present on `Ix` / `Nx` outcomes).

InteractiveErrorBody.description:
Error body for the four interactive-only failures on `POST /validate`
(`mode=interactive`). The default `mode: batch` path never emits these.
  * `unknown_mode` (**400**) — `mode` was neither `batch` nor `interactive`.
  * `interactive_requires_fielded_input` (**400**) — `input` was a string; interactive needs a fielded object.
  * `interactive_needs_locality_scope` (**400**) — `country: fra` interactive requires `city` or `postcode` (no street-leading index).
  * `interactive_resolver_error` (**500**) — the interactive resolver raised.

arrival_point.description: Entrance / access coordinate (arrival point) of the matched premise, returned beside the served coordinate on house-number-level matches when the reference row carries one. With `accuracy_type: rooftop` this is the door/curb point of the same address (useful for delivery and navigation); with `accuracy_type: arrival_point` it simply equals `lat`/`lng`. Omitted when the match is not premise-level or no arrival point is on file — never null.

city.description: Present for countries with regions (USA, CAN).

town.description: Alternative to `city` for countries without regions.

house_number_not_found.description: The house number you sent is not on file for the matched street — either flagged by the matcher itself, or caught by the input-vs-returned comparison (a fallback row carried a different number). standardized keeps YOUR house number in this case; match tier is capped at street_level.

matched_via_alias.description: True when a locality alias (USPS city / CAN community) was used.

city_mismatch_ignored.description: Canada only — matched by province + street + HNO, city name ignored.

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added. Optional but always emitted on a match.

balance.description: Remaining geocode transactions after keyed call.

ForwardGeocodeResponse.description:
Response for `GET /geocode` and `POST /v1/geocode`. A strict whitelist of
geocoding-only fields — every key that can appear is listed below, and no
`/validate` AV field (`status`, `deliverable`, `corrections`,
`match_components`, `match_details`, `match_score`, `match_type`,
`confidence`, `confidence_level`, `input_corrected`, `provided_components`,
`parsed`, `partial_match`, `house_number_not_found`,
`hno_range_verified`, `enrichment`, or any legacy variant) can appear
here. `lat`, `lng`, `accuracy_type`, `point_coordinate`, `standardized`
and `formatted_address` are always present on a 200; the rest — including
the billing tail (`balance`/`validation_credits`/`free_remaining`/
`key_class`/`free_daily_limit`) and the country-conditional fields
(`attribution`, `uprn`, `digipin`, and for Portugal `reasons`,
`nearby_house_numbers`, `approximate`, `resolved_level`,
`resolved_name`) — are emitted only when applicable.

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. Branch on this rather than on `accuracy_type` literals — it stays correct when new tiers are added.

standardized.description: The matched address, componentized. Only the components the match actually resolved are present — an unresolved component (e.g. no `state` for a country that does not use one) is simply absent from the object, never emitted as `null` or `""`.

dependent_locality.description: Royal Mail PAF sub-element (GBR) / secondary locality line. Present only when the matched row carries one — e.g. the village between street and post town ("10 HAYDEN LANE / CHELTENHAM" would otherwise drop it, leaving two same-named streets in different villages indistinguishable).

double_dependent_locality.description: Royal Mail PAF sub-element (GBR), finer than dependent_locality.

dependent_street.description: Royal Mail PAF sub-element (GBR) — a secondary street name.

street_type.description: Thoroughfare type carried in its own DB column rather than folded into `street` (e.g. Malaysia's UPU S42 type).

suburb.description: NZ Post's line between street and post town (NZL). Omitted when it just repeats `city`.

province.description: Province sigla for the mandatory Poste Italiane locality line (ITA).

formatted_address.description: Printable multi-line address block, e.g. for a shipping label.

arrival_point.description: Entrance / access coordinate of the matched premise. Present only when the matched row has one — house-number-level matches — and absent on street/locality fallbacks and when the served coordinate came from a POI. Never `null`; never derived from `lat`/`lng`.

input_modified.description: Lowercase names of the components the engine changed from what the caller sent in a single-line `q=` input (e.g. `["street", "city"]`), deduped. States a fact about the input, not a verdict about the address — it is not a re-admission of the forbidden `corrections` / `input_corrected` AV fields. Present only when non-empty: no key at all when nothing was modified, never an empty array.

attribution.example: Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2026

uprn.description: GBR only. Ordnance Survey Unique Property Reference Number, present when known.

digipin.description: IND only. India Post DIGIPIN, a deterministic 10-character code derived purely from `lat`/`lng` (never from address existence — it says nothing about whether the address itself was verified). Present only when this deployment has DIGIPIN enabled; not guaranteed on every India response even from a deployment that has it enabled (omitted if no coordinate was resolved, or the encoder found none).

reasons.description: PRT only, optional. Present when the point is not a confirmed house: what could not be pinned down (e.g. `house_number_unconfirmed` + `house_number_not_in_reference`, `below_verification_threshold` + `house_number_missing`, or `street_missing` / `fell_back_to_locality` on an approximate point). Same codes as `/validate`.

nearby_house_numbers.description: PRT only, optional. The house number you sent is not in the reference data; names the nearest same-parity numbers that are. The point is then `street_centroid`, or `street_interpolated` between those numbers.

street_postcodes.description: Netherlands only, optional. Present only on STREET-LEVEL answers (`accuracy_type` `street_centroid`, `street_segment_centroid` or `street_interpolated`): the postcodes the matched street covers, each with its house-number range. Sorted by `house_number_from`, then `postcode`; at most 50 entries (see `street_postcodes_total` and `street_postcodes_truncated`). Ranges count numeric house numbers only; addresses whose number carries letters are not counted. Absent on rooftop and other house-number-level answers.

parity.description: Which side(s) of the street the postcode covers within that range.

street_postcodes_total.description: With `street_postcodes`, how many postcodes the street covers (not capped).

street_postcodes_truncated.description: With `street_postcodes`, `true` when the street covers more postcodes than are listed.

postcode_range.description: Netherlands only, optional. Sent with `street_postcodes` when the street covers MORE THAN ONE postcode: the lowest and highest postcode over the whole street (an outer bound, not a continuous run; `street_postcodes` lists the exact ones). In that case `standardized.postcode` carries `text` instead of a single postcode and `standardized.formatted_address` prints it. Check for this field before treating `standardized.postcode` as one postcode.

approximate.description: PRT only, optional. `true` when the point is a town / area centre standing in for the address — a city- or neighbourhood-only request (`street_missing`) or a street that could not be placed (`fell_back_to_locality`). `accuracy_type` is then `locality_centroid` or `admin_centroid`.

resolved_level.description: PRT only, with `approximate`. Which kind of place the point stands for.

resolved_name.description: PRT only, with `approximate`. The place's name as spelled in the reference data.

balance.description: Remaining geocode transactions after a keyed, non-free-tier call.

free_remaining.description: Free calls left today, for anonymous and non-`free_av_geo` free-tier callers.

key_class.description: Present only for verified `free_av_geo` keys — `"free_av_geo"`. See `/check-key`.

free_daily_limit.description: Present only for verified `free_av_geo` keys. Always `1000` (the shared daily allowance).

ReverseResponse.description:
Reverse geocoding response. When the request's `limit=1` (default), the body
is a single flat result. When `limit>1`, the body contains a `results` array
of flat result objects plus `count` and top-level `match_type` / `match_score`
reflecting the best (closest) match.

lat.description: Latitude of the matched address (not the query point).

distance_m.description: Distance in metres from the query point to this result.

point_coordinate.description: `true` when the coordinate identifies one address (`rooftop` or `arrival_point`), `false` for any derived/area tier. **Not yet emitted by `/reverse`** — until it is, derive it from `accuracy_type` (`rooftop` / `arrival_point`).

input_corrected.description: Always `false` for reverse geocoding (input is coordinates, not an address).

state.description: Present for countries with regions (USA, CAN).

query.description: Echo of the effective query parameters (after clamping).

units_charged.description:
Echoes the number of addresses returned (`count`, or `1` when the
body is a flat single result). This equals the trial-key debit;
Stripe-plan keys are debited a flat `1` per request regardless.
Always `1` for RapidAPI traffic.
